## About the position

Description

At the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT), we're on a mission to translate scientific discovery into real world impact. We bring together visionary scientists, technologists, engineers, researchers, educators and innovators to tackle humanity's greatest challenges in four transformative areas:

* Health, Medical Science & Generative Biology
* Food Security & Sustainable Agriculture
* Climate Change & Managing CO2
* Artificial Intelligence & Robotics

This is ambitious work - work that demands curiosity, courage, and a relentless drive to make a difference. At EIT, you'll join a community built on excellence, innovation, tenacity, trust, and collaboration, where bold ideas become real-world breakthroughs. Together, we push boundaries, embrace complexity, and create solutions to scale ideas from lab to society. Explore more at www.eit.org .

Welcome to the Pathogen Project:

Within this ecosystem, the Pathogen Mission exemplifies EIT's commitment to transformative science. It aims to revolutionise the diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases by leveraging whole genome sequencing (WGS)-based metagenomic and pathogen-specific analytical tools. This remit includes the development of a decentralised, sample-to-answer sequencing diagnostic platform for infectious diseases, enabling rapid and accurate analysis of patient samples without prior assumptions. Supported by Oracle Inc.'s cloud-computing scale and security infrastructure, the Pathogen Mission is progressing towards certified diagnostic products for deployment in laboratories, hospitals, and public health organisations worldwide.

Your Role:

At EIT we are seeking an experienced and detailed orientated Senior Scientist, Automated Diagnostic Systems to help develop a novel device-based metagenomic pathogen detection platform within the Pathogen Programme. Working at the intersection of biology, chemistry, and engineering, you will translate molecular biology workflows into automated, integrated diagnostic systems.

You'll lead the development and optimisation of workflows for nucleic acid extraction, purification, library preparation, and sample processing within a fluidic device, helping to reduce technical risk and guide the platform from proof-of-concept through to prototype.

The role involves close collaboration with engineers, chemists, and scientists across disciplines to ensure biological workflows can be robustly implemented within an automated device architecture. We're particularly interested in candidates with experience developing automated molecular diagnostics, analytical instruments, or cartridge-based platforms, and translating manual laboratory processes into scalable automated systems.

Key Responsibilities

* Design and execute robust experiments to generate high-quality data and inform technical decisions.
* Translate molecular biology workflows into automated processes for integration within a diagnostic platform.
* Apply Design of Experiments (DoE) and quantitative methods to optimise workflow performance.
* Develop performance metrics and analytical frameworks to support iterative platform development.
* Identify and resolve bottlenecks, variability, and failure modes across integrated workflows.
* Generate insights that guide system design, including fluidics, reagents, automation, and overall architecture.
* Improve assay robustness, reproducibility, and scalability.
* Collaborate closely with biologists, chemists, and engineers to integrate biological workflows into automated systems.
* Provide technical leadership by defining experimental strategies, prioritising risks, and supporting prototype development.

Requirements

Essential Knowledge, Skills and Experience

* PhD (or equivalent industry experience) in Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, Bioengineering, Biochemistry, or a related discipline.
* Experience developing molecular biology workflows in industrial or translational R&D environments.
* Proven track record of automating or semi-automating molecular biology workflows.
* Experience integrating biological workflows into analytical, diagnostic, or cartridge-based platforms.
* Strong understanding of nucleic acid extraction, purification, and analysis across diverse sample types.
* Ability to design robust experiments and interpret results within complex systems.
* Experience identifying and resolving bottlenecks in integrated biochemical workflows.
* Strong understanding of assay performance, reproducibility, and quantitative development metrics.
* Experience balancing biological requirements with engineering constraints such as fluidics, automation, contamination control, and reagent stability.
* Proven ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams spanning biology, chemistry, and engineering.

Desirable Knowledge, Skills and Experience

* Experience developing automated molecular diagnostic platforms from concept to prototype.
* Experience with cartridge-based sample preparation systems and workflow integration.
* Experience developing integrated analytical or diagnostic instruments.
* Experience automating sequencing library preparation workflows.
* Familiarity with sequencing-based diagnostics, metagenomics, and NGS technologies.
* Experience with Oxford Nanopore sequencing.
* Experience handling challenging clinical samples, including low biomass or inhibitor-rich specimens.
* Experience with microfluidics and miniaturised fluid handling systems.
* Experience collaborating with mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineers.
* Experience applying Design of Experiments (DoE) methodologies.
* Knowledge of surface functionalisation, biomolecule immobilisation, or material-biomolecule interactions.
* Experience evaluating contaminants, inhibitors, and residual reagents within sample preparation workflows.

Key Attributes

Scientific & Technical Expertise

* Innovative scientist with a track record of product development, translational research, patents, or publications.
* Strong systems thinker with experience developing and optimising complex biological and engineering workflows.
* Comfortable working with evolving technologies, technical uncertainty, and data-driven decision making.

Collaboration & Leadership

* Experienced in leading technical projects and working within multidisciplinary teams.
* Strong communicator, able to translate scientific insights into practical technical solutions.
* Collaborative approach with the potential to take on leadership responsibilities as the team grows.

Personal Qualities

* Curious, pragmatic, and evidence-driven.
* Organised and adaptable, with the ability to prioritise effectively in fast-paced environments.
* Resilient team player motivated by developing technologies that can transform clinical diagnostics.

Benefits

Our Benefits:

* Travel allowance
* Annual Bonus
* Pension - Employer contribution 7.5%, minimum employee contribution 5%
* Life Assurance.
* Income Protection
* Private Medical Insurance as standard for you, your partner and any dependents. Including hospital Cash Plan
* Employee discounts
* Electric car scheme

* Cycle to Work Scheme
* Family Planning
* Neurodiversity support including advise and assessments
* Coaching & Therapy services

Working Together - What It Involves:

* You will live in, or within easy commuting distance of, Oxford (or be willing to relocate).

About us:

2Excel Aviation Ltd is an industry leader in specialised and innovative solutions for aviation’s most complex challenges and our success is based on the talented and experienced people that make up our workforce.  We’re now looking to appoint a Finance Assistant to join our friendly Finance team at our Head Office at Sywell Aerodrome.

About the Role:

Reporting directly to the Finance Supervisor, the Finance Assistant will partner closely with our various business units, whilst also contributing to the wider Company finance tasks. The successful candidate will play a crucial role in maintaining the Company purchase ledger, processing invoices and contributing to the overall financial health of the company. There is great scope within this role for future development within the team.

The role’s key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:

* Support all Purchase Ledger and Sales Ledger duties, to ensure the ledgers are accurate, up to date and reconciled.
* Liaise with both internal and external stakeholders, to effectively resolve any queries or disputes.
* Meticulously process both Expenses and Credit Card transactions, making sure all required documentation is obtained and necessary outputs are produced.
* Effectively chase any outstanding customer balances, to ensure payments are received on time, in full.
* Collate, process, and analyse internal cross charges from various departments, in line with month end deadlines.
* Reconciliation and posting of company petty cash accounts, ensuring all documentation is obtained.
* Co-ordinate supplier payments both internally and externally, in a timely manner.
* Communicate information regarding payments and receipts, to enable accurate cash flow forecasting.
* Plan in accordance with month end deadlines to ensure duties are completed on time.
* Support training requirements of administrative duties.
* Compose reports, both regular and ad hoc, to highlight key information.
* Continuously review, challenge, and suggest improvements to systems and processes.
* Support the success of the business, by assisting with other requirements, when needed.

About you:

You’re likely already working in a Finance or accounting setting, or have in the past, and are looking for an exciting challenge. You’ll be a great communicator who has the ability and confidence to communicate at all levels and work effectively with key stakeholders. You’ll have excellent attention to detail and have an analytical approach when reviewing purchase invoices and credit notes. You’ll be able to support the team with ideas and have input into processes to maintain a positive level of change within the Finance Department.

We are particularly looking for candidates who can demonstrate experience in the following:

* Finance, Accountancy or Administrative background
* Previous experience of working with purchase invoices and credit notes
* Experience of managing Sales and Purchase Ledgers, including auditing to ensure data accuracy

What’s on offer:

We can offer you a competitive salary reflective of your experience, 25 days of annual leave from day one which increases with length of service, flexible working arrangements, company pension, Group Life Insurance and private health insurance.

To apply, please upload an up to date CV.  We would also love for you to include a covering letter, telling us how you meet the requirements of the role.

# B1/B2 Licensed Engineers

**Do you want to say you helped put the next-generation UK fighter jet into service?  We’re looking for B1 and/or B2 Licensed Engineers to join our newly created team at Boscombe Down to deliver an exciting engineering programme that will see our Flight Test Aircraft contribute to the development of the UK’s Future Combat Air System (FCAS).**

**About us:**

2Excel is a high-performance aviation services business that specialises in doing difficult things well.   We have experienced significant growth since inception, and that vector shows no sign of slowing down. Spread over multiple sites, engaging in a wide variety of activities including search and rescue, charter, capability development and aircraft maintenance, our people are at the heart of our business and, therefore, our priority.

Since 2019, we have been working on our Excalibur project, a flight test aircraft created as a flying laboratory for combat air technology.  It is part of the UK’s Future Combat Air System (FCAS), which will include the core fighter being developed under the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), as well as a broader range of capabilities such as uncrewed aircraft, information systems and weapon systems.

As we enter the next phase of this project, we are seeking exceptional B1 and/or B2 Licensed Engineers to join our team to support the engineering programme at Boscombe Down in Wiltshire.

**About the role:**

Our Licensed Engineers play a crucial role in ensuring the airworthiness of our aircraft, performing maintenance tasks, and conducting inspections in compliance with regulatory standards and company procedures. Reporting to the Station Engineer, this role will generally work Monday to Friday with flexibility to accommodate emergency situations, unscheduled maintenance or project deadlines.  Key duties will include:

* Conduct scheduled and unscheduled maintenance tasks plus modifications, on our 757 aircraft, including inspections, repairs, and modifications, in accordance with approved data and regulations.
* Perform troubleshooting and fault diagnosis to identify and rectify defects in aircraft systems, avionics, and components.
* Carry out aircraft certification and release to service activities as a B1 and/or B2 Licensed Engineer, ensuring all work is completed to the required standards and documentation is accurately maintained.
* Collaborate with other maintenance personnel, engineers, and support staff to achieve efficient workflow and minimise downtime for aircraft.
* Adhere to all relevant safety protocols, procedures, and regulations, promoting a culture of safety awareness and compliance within the team.
* Flexibility to work at other 2Excel sites in line with business needs.

**About you:**

You’ll be an experienced Licensed Aircraft Engineer, holding a CAA Part 66 B1 and/or B2 Licence.  Experience of large aircraft is essential; experience and/or type rating and recency on Boeing 757 would be extremely advantageous.

You’ll have experience of working in a Part 145 MRO environment, preferably with a good mix of line, base and modification experience.

You’ll have a strong knowledge of aircraft systems, avionics, and powerplants, with the ability to interpret technical manuals and drawings.

You’ll have excellent troubleshooting and diagnostic skills, with a meticulous attention to detail and a commitment to quality outputs.

You’ll be an effective communicator, both verbal and written, and have the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

You will also need to be eligible to hold a UK Security Clearance, which is a requirement of this role.

**What we offer:**

In return, we can offer a generous salary, 25 days holiday per year from day one plus bank holidays, 5% matched Pension scheme, Group Life Insurance, Health and Wellbeing benefits including Health Care Cash Plan and an EAP, and much more.

If required, we can also provide 757 Type Rating training, which will be bonded for a period of 2 years post completion.  At present we are aiming to start this training in Mid May 2027 so looking for candidates able to start shortly before this date.

Apply using our application form and upload your CV.  You are encouraged to use the Covering Letter function to demonstrate how you meet the requirements of the role.

# Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Remote Compute Accounting

## Location

Remote/Flexible; London; Singapore

## Employment Type

Full time

## Department

Verification

## Compensation

* $100K – $200K

OverviewApplication

## **The team**

Some of the most consequential decisions of the AI era will depend on answering one question: can we verify what is happening inside AI datacenters? Answering it could unlock international cooperation, help countries protect their sovereignty, and enable trustworthy adoption of AI in high-stakes industries. Building tools that can earn trust across borders is an urgent technical and political challenge.

SASH’s Verification team builds and tests tools to verify agreements about AI. We prototype new verification mechanisms, lead international research collaborations, and work with policymakers around the world to show what these tools can do and inform how they’re used.

You’d join a small team combining technical expertise with international AI policy experience. Our technical team is led by Pascal Berrang, an Associate Professor at University of Birmingham, and brings experience from the Singapore Government. Our policy team brings experience from Oxford and the Centre for the Governance of AI, while our partners include experts from the Future of Life Institute and the University of Oxford.

## **The problem**

The hardest question in verification is not whether a datacenter is running the model it says it is. It is whether it is also running something else. A cluster can serve declared inference all day and train an undeclared model on the capacity left over.

We are interested in software-only approaches to this problem. If a verifier can keep a cluster's accelerators demonstrably occupied (i.e., their high-bandwidth memory holding the state they claim to hold, their compute answering challenges that cannot be faked or precomputed in advance), then there is no spare capacity for an undeclared training run. Physics supplies the lever: information cannot travel faster than light, and some computations cannot be performed faster than the hardware allows, so the time a cluster takes to answer is itself evidence about what hardware it has and what that hardware is doing.

The nearest concrete version is a memory-state challenge protocol. The prover commits frequently to workload checkpoints, the verifier fires N unique nonces simultaneously, and each device must return a function of its claimed memory state within a deadline (a function designed to demand serious memory bandwidth and matrix multiplication). Round-trip times are recorded and a random sample is proven genuine. A related family, proof of useful work, pushes further: the declared workload's own computation becomes the evidence, so the accounting costs almost nothing to produce.

Compression is one of the open questions: weights or a KV cache engineered for fast lossless decompression would let a prover reconstruct state it was not actually holding, freeing the hardware for whatever else it wanted to do. Showing that workload state cannot be decompressed inside the challenge window, or modifying workloads so that it cannot, would unlock the approach. Beyond that, a prover may hold secret memory capacity in error-correcting-code cells or overprovisioned regions; the challenge has to be designed so honest response time stays feasible; and the deadline has to be short enough to block cheating while surviving network latency and kernel launch times.

## **Your work**

You would own the question of how much of a cluster can be accounted for from outside it, and how little room can be left over.

Concretely, that means designing challenge protocols and then measuring whether real accelerators can satisfy them: microbenchmarking, writing challenge kernels, characterising what high-bandwidth memory can and cannot do under adversarial conditions, and deciding whether the numbers support a claim someone could stake an agreement on. The work sits between two disciplines: measurement is GPU performance engineering, the rest is constructing a hardness assumption and then trying to break it. We expect most candidates to be strong on one side and curious about the other. You'd work alongside cryptographers and hardware-security colleagues, and you'd be expected to publish, including when the answer is that something does not work.

## **Representative projects**

* Implement a candidate challenge function and characterise honest-response latency across real cluster topologies.
* Establish how much spare capacity a cluster could retain while still passing every challenge, then design that margin down.
* Run the adversarial compression study: how much of a frontier model's weights or KV cache can be losslessly decompressed inside a realistic challenge window, and how much hardware does that free up?
* Design and evaluate post-training that measurably raises the cost of compressing weights, without measurably hurting the model.
* Quantify how much memory a prover could plausibly hide, and what protocol changes make hiding it useless.
* Extend the approach from memory occupancy to compute, through proof-of-useful-work schemes where the declared workload's own computation carries the evidence.
* Take the protocol end to end against a live inference cluster and write up what broke.
* Design a red-team/blue-team competition for the protocol: cheap to run, because they need no new hardware.
* Red-team our own timing assumptions.

## **About you**

We are hiring this role at a range of levels. We care more about ability and trajectory than years of experience.

**You may be a good fit if you:**

* Have GPU performance or systems measurement experience (kernels, microbenchmarks, memory hierarchies, distributed timing) or a cryptographic background and a real appetite for getting your hands on hardware.
* Are rigorous about measurement, including about the ways your own measurement can be fooled.
* Can hold an adversary in your head while you optimise something.
* Are comfortable working on a protocol that may turn out not to work, and saying so in public if it does not.
* Thrive in ambiguous, early-stage environments where defining the problem is part of the job.

**Strong candidates may also have:**

* CUDA or equivalent low-level accelerator programming.
* Compression, information theory, or model quantisation experience.
* Background in timing-based protocols, proofs of space or time, or distance bounding.
* Experience characterising hardware you don’t have documentation for.
* Familiarity with LLM inference internals: batching, KV cache management, scheduling.

* Our team is globally distributed, so remote team members should be comfortable maintaining some working-hour overlap with colleagues across regions.

# Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Zero-Knowledge Verification

## Location

Remote/Flexible; London

## Employment Type

Full time

## Department

## Compensation

* Exact salary depends on location and experience, with room to go higher for exceptional candidates $100K – $200K

OverviewApplication

## **The Team**

Some of the most consequential decisions of the AI era will depend on answering one question: can we verify what is happening inside AI datacenters? Answering it could unlock international cooperation, help countries protect their sovereignty, and enable trustworthy adoption of AI in high-stakes industries. Building tools that can earn trust across borders is an urgent technical and political challenge.

SASH’s Verification team builds and tests tools to verify agreements about AI. We prototype new verification mechanisms, lead international research collaborations, and work with policymakers around the world to show what these tools can do and inform how they’re used.

You’d join a small team combining technical expertise with international AI policy experience. Our technical team is led by Pascal Berrang, an Associate Professor at University of Birmingham, and brings experience from the Singapore Government. Our policy team brings experience from Oxford and the Centre for the Governance of AI, while our partners include experts from the Future of Life Institute and the University of Oxford.

## **The problem**

An international agreement on AI is only as broad as what can be verified, and the appetite for verification is growing. In September 2026 Anthropic gave independent third-party evaluators permanent, employee-level access to its systems, and OpenAI said it would match it. Frontier developers now accept that outsiders should be able to check their work.

Between states, the options are cruder: take the operator's word that a datacenter is running a declared, safety-tested model and nothing else, or put inspectors and hardware inside the building. Inspections do not scale, and installing hardware might not be acceptable to every operator.

Zero-knowledge proofs are the one approach that removes both problems at once. The prover can demonstrate a claim — *the committed model produced these output tokens* — while revealing nothing about the weights, and the verifier's trust rests on mathematics rather than on hardware it has to manufacture, ship and guard. Progress here can be deployed immediately, because there is nothing to fabricate and nothing to install.

The catch has always been cost, and the figures usually quoted for it are badly out of date: the literature still puts proving at four orders of magnitude more expensive than the computation being proved. Our own prototype proves a full conversation with an 8-billion-parameter model in about an hour and a half on a single GPU, and most of what is left is ordinary engineering rather than cryptography. Extrapolated to a 405-billion-parameter model, fifty times larger, that is 16 to 24 hours because cost grows far more slowly than the models do.

Verification is also a much friendlier setting for ZKPs than the applications they were designed for. A verifier needs confidence that, say, 99% of compute is used legitimately — and sampling roughly 300 outputs is enough for 95% confidence in that claim. Better still, the sampling can go *inside* a single proof: preliminary work suggests blocks within a transcript can be sparsely sub-sampled, so floating-point matrix multiplication only has to be emulated exactly for a small sample of vector products. For some problems that is a 100,000x saving over a complete proof.

## **Your work**

You would own the line from "this works in a paper" to "a policymaker can rely on this."

Concretely, that means driving down proving cost, closing the gap between what our proofs currently explain and what a frontier inference actually does, and making the resulting system one that a sceptical adversary's technical staff would sign off on. You'd work alongside hardware-security and systems colleagues on the team and with external cryptographers, and you'd be expected to publish since the whole approach depends on other people being able to check it.

## **Representative projects**

* Prove a full inference transcript from a frontier-scale model end to end, and report honestly what it cost.
* Get an open prototype to parity with the best proprietary systems. The most useful thing anyone can do for this field right now is make the state of the art public and checkable.
* Close out the data-preparation path that dominates our current proving time, using the reference-implementation check as a correctness oracle for AI-assisted optimisation.
* Help develop the agenda for where this field goes next, including where AI-assisted research can be pointed at.
* Design and analyse the sub-sampling scheme: what fraction of blocks must be checked, under what adversary model, to bound the information a dishonest prover can smuggle through.
* Bring ZKPs closer to what is deployed today, integrating exact emulation of the hardware's floating-point behaviour, including its rounding, scaling and accumulation, or moving production inference to integer arithmetic with batch-invariant kernels.
* Build proof circuits for low-precision formats such as NVFP4, where "just emulate the hardware" turns into numerical engineering.
* Investigate compute- and memory-exhaustion schemes such as proof-of-useful-work or proof-of-space.
* Hide the model architecture itself, perhaps through proof recursion.
* Red-team our own constraint system.

## **About you**

We are hiring this role at a range of levels, from people early in their research career to people who have shipped proof systems in production. We care more about ability and trajectory than years of experience.

**You may be a good fit if you:**

* Have built something real with a modern proof system (Halo2, Plonky3, STARK-based stacks, or comparable) *or* have deep GPU and ML systems experience and want to learn proof systems on the job. We expect to hire both profiles.
* Are comfortable reasoning about soundness: what an adversary can do, what your assumption actually buys you, and where the argument is critical.
* Can write code that other people will attack, and enjoy that prospect.
* Are willing to do the unglamorous last mile: generalising across model architectures, chasing numerical mismatches, rather than only the interesting part.
* Thrive in ambiguous, early-stage environments where defining the problem is part of the job.

**Strong candidates may also have:**

* Published work in applied cryptography, verifiable computation, or succinct proofs.
* Low-precision numerics experience: rounding modes, accumulation order, and why two GPUs disagree.
* Formal verification experience, especially of a verifier codebase or a protocol.
* Familiarity with lookup arguments, recursion, or folding schemes.
* Experience explaining a cryptographic guarantee to someone who will never read the proof.
* Experience using AI systems as research collaborators on problems where correctness is checkable, and a view on where that works and where it does not.

## **Role Logistics & Benefits**

## **The team**

Some of the most consequential decisions of the AI era will depend on answering one question: can we verify what is happening inside AI datacenters? Answering it could unlock international cooperation, help countries protect their sovereignty, and enable trustworthy adoption of AI in high-stakes industries. Building tools that can earn trust across borders is an urgent technical and political challenge.

SASH’s Verification team builds and tests tools to verify agreements about AI. We prototype new verification mechanisms, lead international research collaborations, and work with policymakers around the world to show what these tools can do and inform how they’re used.

You’d join a small team combining technical expertise with international AI policy experience. Our technical team is led by Pascal Berrang, an Associate Professor at University of Birmingham, and brings experience from the Singapore Government. Our policy team brings experience from Oxford and the Centre for the Governance of AI, while our partners include experts from the Future of Life Institute and the University of Oxford.

## **The problem**

Verifying what happens inside a datacenter running large AI models is the bottleneck on almost every serious agreement about AI — between states, between a regulator and a lab, between a company and the customers it wants to reassure. The obstacle is always the same shape: the party with something to prove cannot hand over its model weights, and the party doing the checking cannot simply take its word.

One solution to this problem puts its trust in hardware: a trusted execution environment isolates a computation and attests to what ran inside it, so a claim about what happened becomes a claim you can check against a chip. Confidential computing exists on current accelerators and runs near production speed.

That unlocks several problems. An audit tells you something about a model, but nothing connects that result to the weights actually being served — attesting the deployed model by weight hash closes the gap between "this model was evaluated" and "you are talking to the model that was evaluated." The most valuable evaluations are built by people who cannot publish their test set, against models whose weights cannot leave the developer; inside an enclave, neither side has to give way. Logs can be attested where they are produced, making usage auditable after the fact without being readable.

## **Your work**

You would own the question of what a chip's word is actually worth, and then build the systems that are worth building on top of it.

Concretely, that means establishing what attestation on current accelerators does and does not prove, designing a registry that lets an outsider check an attested claim without anyone's permission, and making attested pipelines that hold together when someone hostile pulls on them. "It works" and "an adversary cannot make it lie" are different bars, and only the second one counts here. You'd work alongside cryptographers and hardware-security colleagues on the team and with external partners, and you'd be expected to publish since the whole approach depends on other people being able to check it.

## **Representative projects**

* Establish what a GPU confidential-computing attestation guarantees on current hardware, and publish where it breaks.
* Design and build the registry: the attested-result format, the submission path for third-party auditors, and a verification client someone outside the trust chain can actually run.
* Build attested logging inside an enclave, and work out what a privacy-preserving audit over those logs can and cannot establish.
* Run an evaluation end to end under mutual secrecy, with an attestation recording whose code and whose weights were involved.
* Chain attestations across a pipeline so a claim about a final output stays checkable back to its inputs, then find where that chain breaks under production load.
* Get a confidential-computing stack running on accelerators from more than one supply chain.
* Combine hardware attestation with the team's cryptographic work, so a verifier does not have to trust the chip alone.
* Red-team our own attestation chain.

## **About you**

We are hiring this role at a range of levels. We care more about ability and trajectory than years of experience.

**You may be a good fit if you:**

* Have built something real with confidential computing or hardware enclaves (SGX, TDX, SEV-SNP, Arm CCA, GPU confidential computing) or have strong systems security fundamentals and want to learn them on the job.
* Understand attestation chains well enough to know where they carry weight and where they are decoration.
* Are hard to reassure: you read a security claim and look first for what it does not say.
* Can ship an integration across organisational boundaries, which is as much about people as about code.
* Thrive in ambiguous, early-stage environments where defining the problem is part of the job.

* ML inference serving experience and the operational scars of production deployment.

**Job Summary**  
  

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for end-to-end leadership and delivery of complex, high-impact, client-facing implementation projects within an engineering-driven environment. This role independently managers project execution across scope, timeline, budget, and quality, while exercising judgement to balance client objectives, contractual commitments, and technical delivery constraints. 

 

Operating with a high degree of autonomy, the Senior Project Manager leads cross-functional execution across engineering, product, and client stakeholders and is expected to anticipate challenges, drive critical decisions, and escalate strategically when needed. The role is accountable for delivery outcomes, including financial performance, risk management, delivery quality, and client satisfaction, across multiple concurrent projects. 

  
**Responsibilities**   
  

**Client Implementation & Delivery Ownership** 

* Own full lifecycle delivery of multiple concurrent, complex client implementation projects, ensuring alignment to contractual scope, timelines, budget, quality standards, and client objectives

* Serve as the primary point of accountability for project outcomes, exercising sound judgment across delivery quality, financial performance, risk, and client satisfaction

* Translate complex client requirements into structured, executable delivery plans aligned with engineering capabilities, dependencies, and constraints

* Lead projects through successful completion, including testing, client acceptance, production readiness, and transition to ongoing support

 

**Planning, Financial, and Risk Management** 

* Develop and maintain comprehensive project plans, including scope definition, resource strategy, timelines, critical dependencies, and milestone tracking

* Own project financial management, including budget tracking, forecasting, variance analysis, and proactive corrective action

* Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate complex risks across technical delivery, resourcing, client dependencies, and competing priorities

* Govern scope and commercial impacts through structured change control processes, ensuring alignment with contractual commitments and financial objectives

 

**Engineering & Cross-Functional Execution** 

* Partner closely with engineering, product, and executive leadership to coordinate delivery and resolve complex issues across the software development lifecycle

* Anticipate and manage cross-project dependencies, technical constraints, and release timelines to ensure predictable delivery outcomes

* Drive execution across distributed, cross-functional teams without direct reporting authority.

* Monitor project health using defined metrics and delivery trends, implementing corrective actions and escalating material risks as appropriate

 

**Stakeholder & Client Leadership** 

* Act as a trusted senior delivery partner and primary interface for clients, establishing trust and credibility, managing expectations, and navigating complex project situations throughout the project lifecycle

* Communicate project status, risks, financials, trade-offs, and mitigation strategies to internal and external stakeholders, including senior leadership

* Facilitate alignment between technical and business stakeholders to support timely decision making, resolving ambiguity and competing priorities to maintain delivery momentum

* Strengthen client satisfaction and retention through proactive leadership, strategic communication, and consistent delivery excellence

  
**Requirements**   
  

* Demonstrated ability to independently lead multiple complex, high-impact, client-facing projects within a software or engineering environment

* Strong understanding of software development lifecycle (SDLC), implementation delivery models, and the dependencies inherent in enterprise software delivery

* Demonstrated experience managing project scope, financials, risks, dependencies, and delivery outcomes across the full project lifecycle.

* Proven ability to manage competing priorities and navigate ambiguity across concurrent initiatives

* Ability to influence and align cross-functional teams and stakeholders without direct authority

* Demonstrated accountability for delivery quality, financial performance, risk management, and client outcomes;

* Demonstrated ability to mentor project team members, share delivery best practices, and contribute to continuous improvement across the broader project management organization

 

**Technical & Systems Proficiency** 

* Advanced working knowledge of Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, or hybrid methodologies

* Proficiency with project and delivery tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, MS Project, or equivalent)

* Strong familiarity with enterprise software implementations, data integration, system workflows, and complex technical dependencies

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and collaboration tools

 

**AI Skills and Experience** 

* Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI-enabled tools and emerging technologies to improve planning, analysis, documentation, communication, risk identification, workflow efficiency, and decision support while applying appropriate judgment and oversight

* Experience applying AI to improve project delivery efficiency, synthesize complex information, identify risks and dependencies, and support data-informed decision-making.

* Ability to critically evaluate AI-generated outputs for accuracy, relevance, and completeness and apply professional judgment before incorporating outputs into project deliverables or client communications.

* Ability to identify and implement practical opportunities to incorporate AI into project management workflows while adhering to company requirements for data security, confidentiality, privacy, and responsible AI use.

* Demonstrated ability to adapt to evolving AI capabilities and apply new tools and approaches to complex project delivery challenges.

 

**Experience** 

* 7+ years of project management or consulting experience, including significant experience leading complex, client-facing software implementations

* Experience leading enterprise implementations within financial services, alternative investments, or lending platforms strongly preferred

* PMP, PRINCE2, CSM, or equivalent certification preferred

# SURF Material, Welding & NDT Specialist

Namibia

Oil & Gas Upstream

ID : 10747

**Project** Venus Ultra-Deepwater Development

**Location** London, United Kingdom - Contractor's Premises

**Contract Type** Residential Assignment

**Start Date** December 2026 (Subject to Final Investment Decision - FID)

**Duration** 1 to 3 Years

**Renewable** Yes

**Reporting Line** SURF Technical Manager

**Travel Requirements** Frequent missions to fabrication yards, supplier facilities and offshore installation sites.

**Role Overview**

The SURF Materials, Welding & NDT Specialist Engineer is responsible for overseeing all technical activities related to material selection, corrosion, welding and Non-Destructive Testing (NDT/NDE) within the Subsea Umbilicals, Risers and Flowlines (SURF) package of the Venus ultra-deepwater development project offshore Namibia.

The position ensures the technical integrity, quality and compliance of materials, welding processes and inspection activities throughout the Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Installation (EPCI) phases.

The scope includes Steel Lazy Wave Risers (SLWR), rigid flowlines, rigid spools, rigid jumpers and associated subsea structures, incorporating carbon steel, corrosion-resistant alloy (CRA) lined pipes and duplex materials.

The Specialist Engineer acts as the technical reference for the SURF Contractor and its suppliers regarding materials engineering, corrosion management, welding qualification and advanced NDT techniques.

The position also supports the SURF Technical Manager and multidisciplinary project teams, including Subsea Production Systems (SPS), FPSO, umbilical and flexible pipe specialists.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Materials Engineering & Selection**

* Lead and supervise material selection activities for the SURF package.
* Review and approve material specifications, engineering studies and technical documentation.
* Ensure appropriate material selection for ultra-deepwater subsea applications.
* Oversee materials engineering associated with:
  + Steel Lazy Wave Risers (SLWR).
  + Rigid flowlines and rigid spools.
  + Carbon steel (CS) pipelines.
  + Corrosion-resistant alloy (CRA) lined pipes.
  + WOL / MLP / HRB pipe configurations.
  + Duplex rigid jumpers.
  + Associated subsea structures and equipment.
* Verify compliance with applicable project specifications and international standards.
* Review material characteristics, manufacturing requirements and technical acceptance criteria.
* Assess materials and welding consumables used during fabrication.
* Identify potential material-related technical risks and propose mitigation measures.

**Welding Engineering & Qualification**

* Supervise welding engineering activities throughout the SURF EPCI execution phase.
* Review and approve welding procedures and qualification documentation, including:
  + Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS).
  + Welding Procedure Qualification Records (WPQR).
  + Procedure Qualification Tests (PQT).
  + Welding qualification reports.
* Verify compliance with applicable welding standards and project requirements.
* Review welding methods and acceptance criteria.
* Support welding procedure qualification and mechanical testing activities.
* Witness welding operations and welding operator qualification activities when required.
* Assess welding equipment, fabrication environments and associated HSE arrangements.
* Identify welding-related non-conformities and recommend corrective actions.
* Ensure welding processes meet technical, quality and operational requirements.

**Non-Destructive Testing (NDT/NDE)**

* Oversee NDT/NDE activities associated with SURF fabrication and installation.
* Review and approve NDT procedures, inspection methodologies and acceptance criteria.
* Provide technical expertise in advanced inspection techniques, including:
  + Automated Ultrasonic Testing (AUT).
  + Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT).
  + Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD).
  + Inverse Wavefield Extrapolation (IWEX).
* Assess NDT techniques and the qualifications of NDT personnel.
* Review inspection results and technical reports.
* Support qualification and validation of NDT systems.
* Participate in NDT qualification trials and laboratory testing.
* Ensure NDT activities comply with project specifications and applicable standards.
* Support resolution of inspection-related technical issues and non-conformities.

* Ensure material selection is compatible with project corrosion requirements.
* Assess corrosion risks associated with subsea pipelines, risers and jumpers.
* Review corrosion-related technical deviations and derogation requests.
* Support the technical evaluation of CRA lined pipe systems and associated materials.
* Ensure material integrity requirements are maintained throughout fabrication, installation and operation.

  + Heat Treatment.
  + Induction Bending.
  + Pickling.
  + Passivation.
* Verify compliance with project specifications and relevant international standards.

**About Anthropic**

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

**About Beneficial Deployments**

Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.

**About the Role**

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.

The role focuses on clinical development, where we think Claude can help these partners today. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. Much of this work is drug repurposing: testing new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.

You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.

**Responsibilities**

* Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.
* Build and validate tools that help partners find new uses for approved, mostly off-patent medicines in rare and neglected diseases, from literature, omics and patient data, and assemble the evidence so the partner can decide the next step.
* Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.

**You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have**

* Hands-on clinical development experience: designing, running or analysing clinical trials, or assessing clinical evidence to decide which programmes go forward (for example due diligence or asset evaluation). Drug repurposing work as part of that is a strong plus, as is having contributed to a regulatory submission for a trial.
* Comfort with biomedical data: literature, omics, and real-world patient data (health records, registries, claims), ideally inside secure or trusted research environments.
* Strong engineering skills: you can take an LLM-powered tool from prototype to production code, and write evals to measure it.
* Experience working directly with external partners or customers in a technical role.
* Clear written and verbal communication: docs other institutes can use without you, and results clinicians trust.
* A scrappy mentality: you're comfortable in ambiguity, wear several hats, and do what it takes to get a result for a partner.

### **Senior Service Manager - Active UK SC Clearance Required**

**Location:** London, UK (Hybrid - typically 1-2 days per month in office)

### About Appvia

Appvia is a specialist cloud, platform, and solutions engineering consultancy, helping organisations modernise infrastructure, improve reliability, and adopt cloud-native practices that enable long-term, sustainable delivery.

Our engineering capability spans AWS, Azure, platform engineering, networking, software, data, AI, delivery, and managed services.

We work across complex, high-impact environments in both the public and private sector, where security, resilience, operational excellence, and service quality are critical.

### About the Role

We're looking for an experienced Senior Service Manager to join Appvia on a large UK government digital service, at the point where a live service is being replaced by a brand new one.

This role blends three things: designing how a service should be run, managing it day to day, and helping new services move safely into live. People who are brilliant at all three are rarer than a quiet on-call shift, so service design and service management are the priorities. Transition experience is a welcome bonus.

You'll design the support model for the new service, so incidents go straight to the team that owns the component instead of taking the scenic route past every other team first. You'll run incident and problem management, get the problem backlog heading in the right direction (down), and build a technical first line with runbooks people actually use. In time, you'll build a sensible service management culture with SLAs and OLAs, keeping senior stakeholders informed without burying them in status reports.

We want a modern approach. You'll know ITIL well, and you'll also know when to put it back on the shelf. This service is built by agile teams who release often, so we're looking for lightweight change, automation over manual hand-offs, and service readiness built into each team's definition of done rather than checked at the end.

You'll work closely with engineering teams, SREs, the customer's central service management function and frontline operational teams, and be the person who joins them all up. You'll also support and develop a small incident management team.

This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys designing services that work in the real world, then rolling their sleeves up to run them.

### Interview Process - 2 Stage

1. Discovery conversation with Talent Acquisition
2. Final interview with Appvia / customer-facing leadership

### Important

You must be eligible for UK Security Clearance (SC).

## Requirements

### About You

You are an experienced Senior Service Manager who has designed and run live digital services built by agile, multi-team delivery, and who reaches for automation before reaching for another spreadsheet.

**You will bring:**

* Experience designing service and support models for digital services, including who owns what, how incidents are routed and how the service is supported out of hours
* Strong hands-on experience running live services: incident, problem and change management, including major/high-severity incident handling
* A track record of reducing problem backlogs and fixing root causes
* Experience working with agile product and engineering teams in a "you build it, you run it" model
* Experience automating service management, such as alert routing, on-call tooling, ticket integration (e.g. ServiceNow to Jira) and pipeline-based change controls
* Working knowledge of SRE practices such as SLOs, error budgets and post-incident reviews
* Comfort with observability tools such as Dynatrace, Grafana or similar, enough to ask good questions of the data
* Strong understanding of SLAs, OLAs, KPIs and service reporting
* Experience defining operational readiness and service acceptance criteria for new services
* Experience building or improving a first-line or technical triage function, including runbooks and knowledge articles
* Strong ITIL 4 knowledge, applied with judgement rather than by the page
* Experience identifying, managing, and escalating service risks appropriately
* The ability to influence engineering teams, central service functions and senior stakeholders without direct authority
* Experience mentoring or supporting the development of more junior service management colleagues
* A proactive, structured, and pragmatic approach

### Responsibilities

**Service design**

* Design the target support model for a new digital service, so incidents route directly to the team that owns the component
* Define a technical first-line triage capability with runbooks and clear escalation paths
* Agree incident, problem and change SLAs, OLAs and reporting with the customer's central service management function
* Map out-of-hours responsibilities across 24/7 operations and on-call engineering teams
* Build service acceptance criteria into engineering teams' definition of done, covering monitoring, runbooks, alerting and support handover

**Service management**

* Own day-to-day incident and problem management across the live and replacement services
* Lead the response to major and high-severity incidents
* Get root cause work started and completed quickly
* Chair problem reviews and keep service records accurate, so reporting can be trusted
* Agree how live problems get time from engineering teams focused on feature delivery
* Provide clear reporting on service health, performance, risks, and actions
* Support and develop a small incident management team

**Automation and improvement**

* Tune alerting so alerts mean something and reach the right people
* Replace manual escalation with automated alerting and on-call tooling
* Automate the flow between service management and engineering tooling
* Champion lightweight, pipeline-based change over heavyweight approval boards
* Identify opportunities for continual service improvement

**Service transition**

* Plan operational readiness and early life support for a new service going live
* Lead knowledge transfer to support teams before go-live
* Support the decommissioning of the legacy service

### Technical / Service Management Skills

**Core:**

* Service design and support model design
* Incident, Problem & Change Management, including major incident management
* Agile and DevOps ways of working
* Service management automation and tooling integration
* SLA, OLA, SLO and KPI management
* Operational readiness and service acceptance criteria
* Service reporting and governance
* Stakeholder management across engineering, operations and senior customer teams
* Continual service improvement

**Nice to have:**

* Active UK SC clearance
* ITIL 4 or 5 certification
* Service transition and early life support experience
* ServiceNow and Jira, ideally integrated
* Dynatrace, Grafana or similar observability tooling
* PagerDuty, Opsgenie or similar on-call tooling
* SRE experience or certification
* Public sector experience, especially citizen facing digital services
* Experience setting up a service desk or technical first-line function
* Awareness of the cloud technologies underpinning a service (e.g. AWS, Azure)

As we scale, we’re maturing as a business and expanding into new areas across platform engineering, software, data, and AI. We’re intentional about keeping our culture at the heart of it. ## Job Description

**The Role**

We are looking for a practical, technically capable and highly customer-focused **Customer Support Technician** to become our primary day-to-day representative at a major customer site near Cheltenham.

This is much more than a traditional maintenance or technician role. You will be embedded within the customer's operation and will develop a detailed understanding of their test systems, equipment and day-to-day challenges. You will provide first-line technical support, undertake hands-on electrical and mechanical work and act as the link between the customer and Averna's wider engineering organisation.

You will not be expected to know the answer to every problem yourself. An important part of the role is having the technical judgement to investigate issues effectively, recognise when additional expertise is required and engage the appropriate specialists from across Averna.

Just as importantly, you will build relationships across the customer's organisation. Working closely with our Account Manager and engineering teams, you will help us identify where equipment, processes or support could be improved and turn those observations into potential engineering solutions and new opportunities.

For the right person, this is an opportunity to become a trusted technical partner to the customer rather than simply somebody who repairs equipment when it fails.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Customer and Technical Support**

* Act as Averna's primary day-to-day representative at the customer site and build strong working relationships with engineering, production, maintenance and other customer teams.
* Provide first-line support for test systems and associated equipment including both Averna-supplied systems and equipment originally supplied by others.
* Investigate faults and operational issues and establish the appropriate course of action.
* Diagnose faults to module level and, where appropriate, component level using standard electronic test equipment.
* Work closely with Averna engineering specialists to escalate more complex problems and bring the appropriate expertise to bear.
* Develop a strong working knowledge of the customer's equipment, systems and operating environment.
* Help identify recurring issues, weaknesses and opportunities to improve equipment reliability, maintainability, usability and performance.
* Provide a responsive and pragmatic service while recognising the limits of your own knowledge and seeking specialist support where appropriate.

**Hands-on Engineering**

* Undertake electrical wiring, modification, repair and rework activities in accordance with customer requirements and approved engineering information.
* Carry out wiring, looming, crimping, terminating and soldering activities to an appropriate professional standard.
* Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring schedules, general arrangement drawings and other engineering documentation.
* Follow calibration, test and diagnostic procedures accurately and use the results to identify potential equipment failures.
* Use standard instrumentation including DMMs, oscilloscopes and LCR meters to support fault diagnosis.
* Undertake basic mechanical and fabrication activities associated with test equipment including drilling, panel modification, removal of damaged fasteners and thread repair.
* Work with the customer and Averna engineering teams where modifications or repairs require additional design authority, specialist knowledge or engineering approval.

**Customer Development**

* Work closely with the Averna Account Manager to understand the customer's wider objectives, priorities and challenges.
* Identify opportunities where Averna's engineering, test, support or obsolescence capabilities could improve the customer's operation.
* Recognise potential requirements arising from recurring faults, ageing equipment, capacity constraints, process inefficiencies or new programmes.
* Help engineering and sales colleagues understand and develop these opportunities by providing practical insight from the customer environment.
* Support site visits, technical discussions and requirements capture activities where appropriate.
* Contribute to making Averna easier to work with and continually improving the customer's experience of our business.

**Wider Field Support**

Although the role will be predominantly based at the customer site near Cheltenham, there may occasionally be a requirement to support Averna test systems installed at other customer locations.

This may include:

* Supporting ATEC and other test systems at customer sites elsewhere in the UK.
* Occasional travel to European customer locations.
* Working closely with engineering and support colleagues in France and elsewhere within the Averna Group.
* Occasional travel to Toulouse for technical training, knowledge transfer and team activities.
* Occasional visits to Averna's UK operation, currently based in Bournemouth.

The Cheltenham customer site will remain the principal place of work and travel is expected to represent a relatively small proportion of the role.

**About You**

Technical capability is important but **personality, judgement and customer skills are equally important to this position**. You will be comfortable working independently within a customer's organisation and will naturally build relationships with the people around you. You will be curious about how things work and why problems occur rather than simply addressing the immediate symptom. You will have the confidence to take ownership of problems while also having the judgement to recognise when you need help. Averna has considerable engineering expertise available across the wider organisation and we want someone who will make effective use of that expertise rather than feeling they have to solve everything alone.

You will ideally be:

* Outgoing, approachable and comfortable dealing with people at different levels within a customer organisation.
* A good communicator and conversationalist who naturally develops strong working relationships.
* Practical and hands-on with a strong problem-solving mentality.
* Able to work independently and use your own initiative.
* Sensible and pragmatic with good technical judgement and common sense.
* Curious and willing to investigate problems rather than simply follow instructions.
* Confident enough to take ownership but self-aware enough to recognise when specialist expertise is required.
* Customer-focused and motivated by finding better ways of doing things.
* Commercially aware and able to recognise when a technical issue or customer challenge could represent a wider opportunity.
* Comfortable working collaboratively with engineering and sales colleagues across different locations and countries.

**What Success Looks Like**

Success in this role will mean that the customer sees you as their first point of contact when they have a test equipment problem or need help finding a better way of doing something.

You will solve many problems yourself and know when to bring in Averna's wider engineering capability for those you cannot. You will understand the customer's equipment and operation well enough to spot issues before they become major problems and identify opportunities for improvement.

Above all, you will help build a strong day-to-day relationship between the customer and Averna – combining responsive local support with access to the capabilities of a much larger international engineering organisation.

## Qualifications

**Technical Skills and Experience**

We would expect you to have a good foundation in electrical/electronic engineering with practical experience of maintaining, supporting, manufacturing or modifying complex electrical or electronic equipment.

Ideally you will have:

* An HNC/HND or equivalent qualification in electrical, electronic or a related engineering discipline. Relevant practical experience may also be considered.
* Experience of fault-finding on electrical or electronic systems to module level with component-level diagnostic capability advantageous.

* Strong practical wiring skills including looming, crimping, terminating and soldering.
* The ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring schedules, system diagrams and general arrangement drawings.
* Experience working to recognised wiring and workmanship standards with IPC-WHMA-A-620 certification desirable.
* Good basic mechanical and fabrication skills associated with the modification and repair of test equipment.
* An understanding of automated test systems and the ability to run and interpret test programmes as part of system fault diagnosis.

Experience in one or more related engineering disciplines such as control systems, power electronics, electromechanical systems, instrumentation, RF or communications would be advantageous but is not essential. Previous experience within aerospace, defence, manufacturing, test engineering or another highly regulated engineering environment would also be beneficial.

## **The Opportunity**

This is a high-impact opportunity to work directly alongside one of Banyan’s seasoned Operating Leaders, each overseeing a portfolio of software businesses in a buy, hold and grow investment model. As **Chief of Staff**, you become a trusted right hand to your Operating Leader and a close working partner to the CEOs and functional leaders across their companies.

The role is deliberately broad. Rather than a fixed rotation, you will move across multiple operating companies and business problems: shaping a go-to-market plan for one company, improving customer onboarding at another, or standing up the first 100 days of a newly acquired business. You will gain exposure to software M&A, but the core of the job is hands-on value creation and operating work. You own initiatives end to end.

The **Executive Leadership Program** (ELP) runs two years. Development is intentional. You will work through a range of experiences spanning go-to-market, M&A, customer, and finance priorities portfolio-wide, plus gain hands-on leadership reps, with regular check-ins and development opportunities to ready you for your next role. High performers move from the ELP program into a CEO or C-suite role within a Banyan operating company, or into a leadership role at Banyan Software HQ.

For those who want to learn how great vertical software businesses are built and run, and who want the fastest path available to running one themselves, this is the job.

## **What You’ll Gain**

* **A cohort of high-calibre peers**. You grow and learn alongside other ELPs at Banyan, building a long-term network of future operators.
* **Direct apprenticeship with senior operators**. You will work very closely with an Operating Leader and see first-hand how experienced leaders make decisions across different software businesses.
* **Dedicated development support**. External executive coaching in Year 2, plus mentorship from Operating Leaders with decades of software experience.
* **The fastest track we offer to running a business**. High performers move directly from this program into a C-suite seat inside a Banyan operating company or a leadership role at HQ. It is not guaranteed, performance decides placement, but it is the first place Banyan looks when those seats open and we have a strong track record of placing CEOs through our ELP.
* **Real operating reps, not case reps**. You carry a genuine initiative inside a live business and leadership-level stretch assignments, decisions that show up in a P&L.

## **What You Will Own**

### **Portfolio Value Creation**

* Partner with CEOs and functional leaders across multiple operating companies to identify priorities and implement the Banyan Operating System, turning strategy into measurable operational improvements.
* Lead high-impact, cross-functional projects across product, go-to-market, sales, marketing, pricing, and customer success as the right hand to Leader.

### **M&A and Integration**

* Gain exposure to Banyan’s acquisition process, including value-creation plan framing during diligence.
* Support integration planning and onboarding for newly acquired businesses, helping establish operating rhythms and priorities while respecting what already makes each business work.
* Help execute the value-creation plan once a deal closes, turning the diligence thesis into the specific operating bets a business needs to win in year one.

### **Executive Partnership**

* Support your Operating Leader on critical initiatives, executive decision-making, and cross-company collaboration, frequently influencing outcomes without formal authority or direct reports.
* Build the judgment, breadth, and pattern recognition required for future general management by working different business problems across a portfolio of vertical software companies.

### **Must-Haves**

* Recently graduated from a top MBA program. This cycle is not open to first-year MBA students.
* 2–5 years of pre-MBA experience in an operating role (product, business operations, portfolio operations, or value creation), management consulting, private equity, or investment banking, with a demonstrated record of owning measurable outcomes.

* Experience in software, SaaS, or another recurring revenue business. Familiarity with vertical software economics is an advantage.

What’s ahead — and why it’s an exciting time to join the team: 

Building agentic AI with advanced orchestration (multi-agent workflows, tool use, evaluation loops) that turns complex talent data into decisions.
Training and fine-tuning our own models on unique data about jobs, skills and tasks, and benchmarking them against the best in our market.
Joining an award-winning AI team (ACM RecSys Challenge 2026) that turns new ideas into innovative solutions with scientific rigour.
Sharing our work and learning from industry peers through challenges, conferences and publications.

About the Team
The Data Science team builds the AI models behind Beamery's Data Foundry, the common data and AI layer powering all Beamery products, and works hand in hand with the product teams to empower their features with AI (such as Talent Match and recommendations). You will join the team as a Senior Data Scientist and own our matching, recommendation and taxonomy mapping models, working closely with the product engineering teams that bring them to our customers. You will be responsible for the full cycle of your work, from defining how quality is measured and designing the models to running robust scientific experiments, tracking technical and business metrics, and writing and reviewing code. Build, improve and own our matching and recommendation models (e.g. candidate to job matching, internal mobility recommendations etc.).
Apply an evaluation-first mindset: build golden datasets from real recruiter and user decisions, define quality metrics, design and run robust scientific experiments, track and report both technical and business metrics (using LLM-as-a-judge and human feedback), and communicate results and metrics clearly to the product teams.
Write clean and tested Python code using AI coding agents (such as Claude Code or Codex), and review code with care, both from your peers and from AI agents, so the team's codebase stays consistent, readable and safe.
Follow recent research (e.g. LLMs, embeddings, recommender systems, explainability, model evaluation) and bring the most relevant ideas into our product roadmap.
Document your work and present it clearly to product, engineering and business stakeholders, and contribute to the team's research visibility (such as challenges, conferences and publications).

A minimum of 2-4 years of experience as a Data Scientist, Senior Data Scientist (or a similar role) in an AI startup or an AI team, with a dynamic environment and a variety of use cases.
Strong experience with recommender systems, search, ranking or matching (e.g. learning-to-rank, scoring models, Gradient Boosting Trees, embedding models).
Fluency in evaluation: designing datasets and quality metrics (such as AUC, NDCG, precision and recall), and using LLM-as-a-judge and human feedback.
A strong foundation in NLP and GenAI, including Transformers, LLMs and embedding models (training or fine-tuning them is a strong plus).
High-quality software development skills in Python (clean design, testing, packaging, maintainable code etc.), practical knowledge of CI/CD, and hands-on experience with agentic coding, with the judgement to know when AI-generated code is right or wrong.
The ability to simplify complex problems, to work with ambiguity, and to collaborate with data scientists, engineers, product managers and business stakeholders.
A Master's degree or PhD, or equivalent experience, in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics or a related field.
Nice to Have
Experience with explainable or conversational recommendations.
Experience in HR Tech, talent acquisition or workforce data.
Publications, open-source contributions or strong results in ML challenges (e.g. RecSys, Kaggle).

The chance to own core AI models that are used by some of the world's most forward-thinking organisations.
A team that publishes, competes and is recognised in the research community, while shipping real products.
Work with the latest AI technologies and tools, including AI coding agents as part of the daily workflow.
Close collaboration with experienced data scientists, QA, platform and product engineers.

## Description

Specialized in civil engineering and engineering structures, Bouygues Travaux Publics is one of the world leaders in the fields of land use planning and sustainable infrastructure construction. Bouygues Travaux Publics is committed to diversity and is open to all talents.

  

Hinkley Point C (HPC) is one of the UK’s largest and most complex infrastructure projects and will play a major role in the UK’s transition to a low-carbon energy future.

Bouygues Travaux Publics and Laing O’Rourke are working together through the BYLOR joint venture to deliver the main civil engineering works at Hinkley Point C, with a contract value of more than £2.8 billion.

BYLOR is delivering construction on an exceptional scale, combining major civil engineering expertise with innovative construction methods and technology. The project has already achieved significant engineering milestones, including breaking the UK record for the largest continuous concrete pour.

## The Role

We are looking for a Quality Engineer to join the BYLOR team at Hinkley Point C.

Supporting the Quality Manager, you will play an important role in implementing and maintaining the project's quality management arrangements and ensuring that construction activities, documentation and records meet the required standards.

Working closely with construction teams, suppliers and the Client, you will provide practical quality support throughout delivery – from Inspection & Test Plans and quality records through to non-conformance management, continuous improvement and final handover.

## Key Responsibilities

### Quality Management & Assurance

* Support the implementation of the BYLOR Quality Management System across project teams and suppliers.
* Communicate and cascade project quality requirements, including plans, procedures, guidance and templates.
* Provide practical quality guidance and support to construction and delivery teams.
* Develop and deliver quality briefings and training materials where required.
* Promote project management policies, quality objectives and key performance indicators.

### Quality Documentation & Records

* Provide guidance and review quality deliverables including Quality Plans, Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs), quality records and record templates.
* Review and approve quality records forming part of the project's Lifetime Quality Records for Client acceptance.
* Ensure records provide appropriate traceability and evidence of completed works.
* Support teams in maintaining complete, accurate and compliant quality documentation throughout construction.

### Non-Conformance & Continuous Improvement

* Support the effective management of non-conformances (NCRs) relating to products, materials and construction processes.
* Ensure causes are appropriately identified and that corrections and corrective actions are defined, implemented and closed out.
* Intervene where the quality of works is at risk or has been adversely affected.
* Escalate significant quality issues to senior management where appropriate.
* Identify opportunities for improvement and support teams in implementing agreed actions.
* Monitor quality outputs and KPIs to identify trends and opportunities for continuous improvement.

### Handover & Completion

* Support and track the handover process as rooms, areas and buildings approach completion.
* Ensure the required quality records are complete and available to support handover.
* Work with project teams to identify and close outstanding quality-related works and documentation.
* Support the progressive completion and acceptance of project records by the Client.

## Essential Skills & Experience

* Previous experience within a Quality Engineer, Quality Assurance, Quality Control or similar construction/engineering role.
* Experience working within a construction, civil engineering or infrastructure environment.
* Understanding of quality management processes and construction quality documentation.
* Experience working with Inspection & Test Plans, quality records and/or non-conformance processes.
* Strong attention to detail and an understanding of the importance of traceability and accurate record keeping.
* Ability to communicate effectively at all levels, including with construction teams, suppliers and Client organisations.
* Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
* Ability to follow established processes while taking a proactive approach to resolving quality issues.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Good computer literacy, including Microsoft Office.

## Desirable Skills & Experience

* Previous experience on a major infrastructure, civil engineering, energy or nuclear project.
* Knowledge of ISO 9001 and Quality Management Systems.
* Experience managing or supporting NCRs and corrective actions.
* Experience producing or reviewing Inspection & Test Plans.
* Experience with Lifetime Quality Records, handover documentation or completion processes.
* Experience working with complex supply chains, subcontractors and suppliers.
* Membership of, or progress towards membership of, a relevant professional quality or engineering body.

## Location

The role will be predominantly site-based at Hinkley Point C in Somerset, with visits to external facilities and suppliers where required.

## Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to develop your Quality career on one of Europe's most significant infrastructure and nuclear construction programmes, gaining exposure to complex civil engineering works and some of the highest standards of quality assurance and traceability within the construction industry.
