## Company Description

At Nielsen, we are passionate about our work to power a better media future for all people by providing powerful insights that drive client decisions and deliver extraordinary results. Our talented, global workforce is dedicated to capturing audience engagement with content - wherever and whenever it’s consumed. Together, we are proudly rooted in our deep legacy as we stand at the forefront of the media revolution. When you join Nielsen, you will join a dynamic team committed to excellence, perseverance, and the ambition to make an impact together. We champion you, because when you succeed, we do too. We enable your best to power our future.

## Job Description

**This position can be done remotely within the UK. A central-London office is also available for hybrid work if preferred. You will be part of a friendly, international team.**

**Job Summary**

The Senior Legal Counsel, Privacy and Data Protection will provide sophisticated, practical, and business-oriented legal advice on EU/EEA privacy and data protection matters across Nielsen’s products, services, commercial relationships, and internal operations. This role will independently manage complex privacy workstreams, support Nielsen’s European privacy program, and serve as a trusted advisor to local sales and business teams. The role will work closely with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and Legal colleagues across jurisdictions.

* Provide senior legal guidance on EU/EEA privacy compliance, data governance, and risk mitigation for business operations, products, partnerships, and commercial transactions.
* Apply in-depth knowledge and experience to solve complex privacy and commercial legal problems, using best practices and a practical understanding of Nielsen’s business.
* Work independently with minimal guidance, lead smaller projects and complex workstreams, and act as a resource for colleagues with less experience.
* Draft, review and negotiate complex data protection exhibits on both the buy-side and sell-side.
* Build consensus among stakeholders by explaining complex, difficult, or sensitive privacy and data protection issues in clear, actionable terms.

**Responsibilities**

* Provide day-to-day legal advice on the EU/EEA General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), applicable national implementing laws, European Data Protection Board (EDPB) guidance, supervisory-authority decisions, ePrivacy requirements, marketing and consumer protection rules, and other relevant European data protection and digital regulations.
* Maintain deep practical knowledge of EU/EEA privacy and data protection requirements and translate legal developments into clear, actionable guidance, contract language, policies, notices, processes, and implementation requirements for local and global stakeholders.
* Draft, review, and negotiate data processing agreements, data protection exhibits, data sharing and data use agreements, data transfer arrangements, and related privacy provisions in commercial contracts, representing Nielsen on both the buy-side and sell-side.
* Support local sales and business teams on privacy aspects of customer agreements, proposals, product offerings, data services, partnerships, and other commercial opportunities, providing timely and commercially practical advice.
* Conduct and oversee privacy impact assessments (PIAs/DPIAs), transfer impact assessments, legitimate interest assessments, and other privacy risk assessments for products, features, data uses, partnerships, and operational initiatives.
* Conduct privacy due diligence on third parties, vendors, customers, and strategic partners, including reviewing questionnaires and security materials, assessing processing activities and data flows, identifying gaps, negotiating remediation, and supporting ongoing oversight.
* Advise on advertising technology, audience measurement, analytics, identity, cookies, pixels, SDKs, targeted advertising, consent and preference management, data monetization, and related media and marketing data practices. Experience in adtech or media technology is strongly preferred.
* Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Information Security, Procurement, Sales, Marketing, and other stakeholders to assess proposed data collection, use, disclosure, retention, and deletion activities and to support compliant product launches and operational changes.
* Communicate with, or support communications with, local data protection authorities and other supervisory authorities as required, including in connection with regulatory inquiries, consultations, complaints, audits, filings, investigations, and data incidents.
* Support privacy incident and data breach response, data subject rights escalations, regulatory inquiries, audits, and other privacy compliance matters in coordination with local business teams, security, legal, and outside counsel.
* Contribute to and improve privacy program materials, including policies, procedures, playbooks, templates, training, records of processing, data inventories, data retention requirements, and compliance reporting.
* Monitor developments in EU/EEA and national privacy law, enforcement trends, and related digital regulation; assess their impact on Nielsen’s business and communicate recommendations to stakeholders.

## Qualifications

* Extensive experience practicing privacy, data protection, technology, commercial, or related legal work in-house, with a track record of producing high-quality independent work.
* Law degree or equivalent legal qualification; qualification or admission in the UK is required, consistent with the requirements for the role.
* Deep, practical knowledge of the GDPR and applicable national privacy and data protection laws in at least one relevant European jurisdiction, with the ability to apply requirements across products, contracts, and business processes.
* Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing DPIAs/PIAs, transfer impact assessments, legitimate interest assessments, and privacy risk assessments, including documenting risks and tracking mitigations.
* Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating DPAs, data protection exhibits, and other privacy-related contract terms, including experience advising both buyers/customers and sellers/providers of data or services.
* Experience advising business, sales, product, technology, or commercial teams on complex privacy issues and translating legal requirements into practical, commercially workable solutions.
* Experience engaging with or supporting communications to supervisory authorities, regulators, or other public-sector stakeholders is preferred and may be required for certain matters.
* Strong legal research, writing, negotiation, analytical, and issue-spotting skills, with the ability to exercise sound judgment and build consensus among diverse stakeholders.
* Excellent written and verbal English communication skills; fluency in an additional European language is a plus.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* CIPP/E certification is greatly preferred, but it is not a hard requirement. CIPM, CIPT, or an equivalent privacy credential is also a plus.
* Adtech, martech, media measurement, audience analytics, data licensing, or digital advertising experience is strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of U.S. privacy and data protection requirements, including U.S. state privacy laws and the CCPA/CPRA, is an advantage.
* Knowledge of APAC privacy and data protection regulations—particularly India’s Digital Personal Data Protection framework, Australia’s Privacy Act and Australian Privacy Principles, or South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act—is an advantage.
* Familiarity with international data transfers, standard contractual clauses, cross-border data sharing, consent and preference management, privacy management tools, data mapping, and records of processing activities.

This directorate is responsible for the NSTA’s activities in support of decommissioning and leading our work with the UK service sector. It is also the Authority’s focal point for engagement on culture change within the industry, working with operating and service sector companies to promote greater collaboration.

The NSTA Decommissioning Team works with industry, through a combination of regulating and influencing, to minimise the cost and emissions impact of decommissioning; and support the repurposing of infrastructure particularly in advancement of energy transition opportunities.

This is done through interacting closely with industry to deliver the post hydrocarbon phase of the life cycle of offshore oil and gas infrastructure, supporting re-use and repurposing where appropriate and delivering cost effective decommissioning as required. The NSTA is a statutory consultee for OPRED on Decommissioning Programmes (DPs) and works closely with other regulatory and industry bodies. They are also the regulator for well decommissioning, which represents almost half of the forecasted decommissioning spend for the UKCS.

Working with industry and stakeholders to identify and deliver a 35% decommissioning cost reduction is a key priority. This is driven by developing industry benchmarks and cost estimates and promoting and influencing change in the way work is planned and delivered.

**Brief overview of role**

The NSTA decommissioning team’s role is to ensure that decommissioning is carried out cost effectively in accordance with regulatory requirements consistent with the OGA Strategy which includes assisting the Government with meeting its net zero target and enabling the energy transition

The decommissioning stewardship engineer role is a primary focal point with UKCS operators during late life operation and decommissioning planning and execution phases. The role consults and interacts closely with a wide range of operators/licensees and has responsibility for understanding and driving operators decommissioning performance improvement and cost efficiencies consistent with the full spectrum of the NSTA objectives and decommissioning strategic priorities. A combination of influence and regulatory activities will be undertaken. The role coordinates, monitors and verifies decommissioning plans, decommissioning readiness and regulatory compliance utilising a wide range of tools, including performance metrics, benchmarks and analysis of industry performance and costs. The role will identify and steward delivery of “tactical” interventions and performance improvement / cost reduction actions and plans with the operators. The role coordinates all necessary input from other NSTA directorates and spans the full decommissioning work breakdown structure.

The development of a capable UKCS decommissioning supply chain is key to delivery of the objective. The role interfaces closely with the NSTA supply chain team and coordinates necessary input from the supply chain in the process of stewardship.

The role acts as a formal consultee in a number of areas and specifically UKCS Decommissioning Programmes as part of OPRED’s regulatory consultation process plus Well decommissioning and PWA consents.

The role will report to the NSTA decommissioning manager who has responsibility for UKCS decommissioning cost stewardship.

**Detailed job description and key responsibilities**

1. Analysing operator decommissioning performance, cost and activity data across the full work breakdown structure to develop insights to support recommendations and decisions in support of achieving sustainable performance improvement and cost efficiency in line with NSTA’s objectives through late life operations into decommissioning.
2. Understand operator strengths and weaknesses and agree tailored stewardship engagement plans with NSTA decommissioning manager based on materiality and full range of considerations; supporting the operator in defining decommissioning plans consistent with legislative requirements and the NSTA’s strategic priorities for decommissioning.
3. Understand and support the NSTA’s Measured Escalation Process for operators who do not deliver on their Stewardship and/or Regulatory obligations, with increased focus or engagement (as applicable) in such instances.
4. A similar function is provided for decommissioning Pipeline Works Authorisations (PWA) consents
5. Review Decommissioning Programmes (DP) as part of the OPRED public consultation process and provide feedback on the DP to the NSTA approver based on cost forecast and identifying any alternatives to decommissioning (including potential re-use/repurposing opportunities).
6. Assist in preparing and delivering Operator review meetings to review and influence their decommissioning activities; decommissioning plans; cost performance and forecasts; promote collaboration opportunities.
7. Regular interaction with the NSTA’s well decommissioning, asset transition and supply chain teams to identify, understand and support cost-effective decommissioning solutions that align with our requirements in these areas.

  Research roles at UKTL utilise our cutting-edge lab environment to test communications systems to their limits in new and novel ways.

  As a graduate in security research and testing, you'll join one of our specialist security research focused teams:

  + Penetration and Cyber Security Testing
  + Vulnerability Research
  + Cyber Security and Privacy Research

  You'll work on real-world challenges affecting national communications infrastructure, helping to identify critical security issues, and improve the resilience of communications products.

  You'll receive structured development, mentoring and technical training throughout the two-year programme, giving you the opportunity to develop specialist expertise in security research and telecoms.

  **Your work could include**

  + Security testing of communications technologies
  + Discovering and analysing new vulnerabilities
  + Developing bespoke research tooling
  + Conducting novel telecoms research on niche equipment
  + Investigating how communications systems behave under real-world attack scenarios

  + Attend a virtual first-stage interview

# **Technical Program Manager – WAN**

## **About Nscale**

Nscale is the GPU cloud engineered for AI. We provide cost-effective, high-performance infrastructure for AI start-ups and large enterprise customers. Nscale enables AI-focused companies to achieve superior results by reducing the complexity of AI development. Our GPU cloud bolsters technical capabilities and directly supports strategic business outcomes, including cost management, rapid innovation, and environmental responsibility.

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

## **About the Role**

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager – WAN to lead the planning, coordination, and delivery of Nscale's wide-area network across Europe. You'll make sure our backbone, interconnects, and new site connectivity are delivered on time, at scale, and with high reliability.

You'll sit within our Deployment organisation, a build org that owns every step from hardware arrival through to customer acceptance, and drive cross-functional programmes spanning Network Engineering, Data Centre Operations, carriers, and commercial teams. The role involves regular travel to sites and partners.

## **What You'll be Doing**

* Drive end-to-end WAN programme delivery, including backbone expansion, new site and region bring-up, capacity upgrades, and network optimisation.
* Build and manage detailed programme plans, tracking dependencies, identifying risks early, and keeping delivery on schedule.
* Coordinate Network Engineering, Infrastructure, SRE, Procurement, and external vendors to deliver against milestones.
* Manage carriers, dark fibre and wavelength providers, IXPs, and hardware vendors through ordering, provisioning, and issue resolution.
* Make sure WAN deployments meet performance, reliability, and scalability requirements before they go into production and are handed to customers.
* Put in place processes, tools, and reporting that improve execution, visibility, and predictability.
* Give clear, regular updates to leadership and stakeholders on progress, risks, and outcomes.

## **About You**

* 5+ years in technical programme or project management, ideally in networking or infrastructure.
* Experience delivering large-scale WAN, telecom, or data centre interconnect programmes, ideally at a hyperscaler or major network vendor (e.g. Microsoft, AWS, Oracle/OCI, Cisco).
* Solid understanding of WAN concepts: BGP and routing, capacity planning, fibre, DWDM, peering, and transit.
* Proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder programmes with strong planning, risk management, and dependency tracking.
* Experience working with carriers, ISPs, and infrastructure vendors.
* Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
* Willingness to travel across Europe as needed.

## **Nice to Have**

* Experience in hyperscale or cloud infrastructure environments.
* Familiarity with AI/ML or HPC infrastructure requirements.
* Experience with network deployment at global scale across multiple countries.
* PMP, PgMP, or similar certification.

## **Why this role matters**

Our WAN connects every Nscale site to our customers. This role decides how quickly new capacity comes online and how reliably it performs once it does.

# Full-Stack React Developer — Interactive Web Games & AI

EngineeringRemoteLong-term remote, 30–40 hours/week

## About Odeum

Odeum is building a **Narrative Learning Platform** that turns educational goals into interactive, story-driven adventures.

Teachers use **Odeum Studio** to create learning experiences with AI. Students then play those experiences directly in their web browser — exploring scenes, interacting with characters, completing quests, making choices, and learning through the story.

We're looking for a strong developer to work directly with the founder and help take ownership of the continued development of **Odeum Studio and our web-based game experience**.

This is intended to be a **long-term role**, not a short freelance project.

## What You'll Work On

You'll work across two connected parts of the product:

### Odeum Studio

Our React-based application where teachers create and edit AI-generated learning adventures.

### Web Game Runtime

The browser-based experience where students actually play those adventures.

A major part of the role will be expanding the gameplay capabilities of the web experience.

Examples of the kinds of things you may work on include:

* Character movement and animation
* Interactive objects and environments
* Scene transitions
* Dialogue and character interactions
* Quest mechanics
* Player actions and choices
* Game state and progression
* New gameplay mechanics
* Asset loading and management
* Improving game performance
* Responsive gameplay across different screen sizes

You'll also work on Studio itself, APIs, and other parts of the platform depending on your experience.

## Current Tech Stack

Our current web application uses:

* React
* TypeScript / JavaScript
* Tailwind CSS
* Zustand
* Framer Motion
* REST APIs
* AI-assisted development tools

The current game renderer uses regular HTML/CSS elements inside React.

Characters, backgrounds, and objects are rendered as positioned sprites in a scene. As our gameplay becomes more sophisticated, we may evolve the renderer or introduce technology such as:

* PixiJS
* Phaser
* Canvas / WebGL
* Three.js
* another appropriate browser game framework

We have **not predetermined the answer**.

Part of this role is helping us determine the right architecture as the product evolves.

## What We're Looking For

You should be very comfortable with:

* React
* JavaScript / TypeScript
* HTML / CSS
* Application state management
* APIs
* Git
* Debugging complex applications

We're particularly interested in developers who have built **interactive applications rather than only standard websites or CRUD applications**.

Experience with any of the following is valuable:

* PixiJS
* Phaser
* Three.js
* Canvas
* WebGL
* Browser games
* Interactive simulations
* Game development
* Animation systems

You do **not** need experience with every technology above.

We're more interested in your ability to learn quickly and solve interactive engineering problems.

## Full-Stack Experience

Backend experience is valuable but isn't required to be your strongest skill.

Our broader platform includes APIs, AI generation pipelines, and AWS infrastructure.

Experience with any of the following is a plus:

* Node.js
* REST APIs
* AWS
* S3
* DynamoDB
* Serverless applications
* AI / LLM APIs
* Structured JSON pipelines

## Bonus Skills

These are helpful but **not required**:

* Unity / C#
* Game engine architecture
* Quest or dialogue systems
* AI-generated applications
* Educational technology
* Developer tools or visual editors

## AI-Assisted Development

We actively use AI to accelerate development.

You should be comfortable using tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, or similar tools where they improve productivity.

We're not looking for someone who simply asks AI to generate code.

We're looking for someone who understands software engineering and can use AI to **build faster while maintaining good architecture and code quality**.

## What It's Like Working With Us

Odeum is an early-stage startup, so this isn't a position where you'll simply receive tickets and implement them.

You'll work directly with the founder on product and engineering decisions.

You'll have the opportunity to:

* Own significant parts of the product
* Recommend architectural improvements
* Introduce better engineering practices
* Build new gameplay systems
* Experiment with new technologies
* Help determine how our web game engine evolves

We're looking for someone who enjoys both **building things quickly** and **turning successful prototypes into reusable systems**.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone interested in a long-term relationship who can grow with the product.

## What Matters to Us

We're less interested in degrees, certifications, or knowing every technology on our list.

We care about whether you can:

**Build. Solve problems. Learn quickly. Communicate clearly. Take ownership.**

If you're a strong React developer who wants to move deeper into interactive experiences and browser game development, we'd especially like to hear from you.

## Apply for this role

Fields marked \* are required. Your resume is scanned before anyone opens it.

### Questions about this role

Please start your application with the word ODEUM in the first answer so we know you read the complete posting.

Tell us specifically what you built yourself. GitHub links, live applications, games, demos, videos, or portfolio links are all welcome.

It's completely fine if you don't have experience in every category.

For example: Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Lovable, ChatGPT, or others. Tell us briefly how you use them in your normal development workflow.

Imagine you're building a browser-based 2D experience with React and TypeScript that includes animated characters, movement, and interactive objects.

# # Technical Product Owner, DevOps Platform - UK

Product Delivery - London, Greater London (Remote)

About OneView Commerce

For retailers with thousands of shops, commerce platforms have historically fallen into two categories, each with significant drawbacks. Web-native platforms move fast but were never built for a shop floor. Legacy store systems were built for the shop floor but take a year to change anything. OneView Commerce is the third option: a headless commerce platform for physical retail that lets the world's largest retailers innovate just as quickly as the smaller ones. We ship store experiences that deploy fast out of the box, and we give retailers the freedom to build their own on top of a headless transaction engine engineered for the physical store rather than the browser.

Our customers are global retailers who build on OneView because it lets them keep moving: new journeys, new channels, and new store formats ship continuously rather than waiting on the next multi-year program.

Founded in 2010 to close the gap between fast-moving e-commerce and slow-moving in-store systems, OneView's founding principle is a single view of customers, orders, and inventory throughout the shopping journey. That remains our mission as we enable retailers to deliver exceptional store experiences that build loyalty.

We are a remote-first team with Viewers working across the globe, and we operate as a trusted provider of digital commerce systems for leading retailers.

Position summary

OneView is looking for a Technical Product Owner with a DevOps engineering background to own the flow of work into our DevSecOps team. The team builds and secures the platform every other team here depends on, which makes it the most contended team in the company. Work reaches the team from two sources: requests from software engineering, QA, agile delivery, product support, customer implementation, security, and leadership; and the Platform Engineering roadmap, which includes building our internal developer platform (IDP). You decide what the team takes on, in what order, and what it declines, and you will say "no" and "not yet" more often than "yes".

You report to the Sr. Director of Platform Engineering, who leads the DevSecOps pillar and sets product vision, strategy, and the roadmap, with input from the VP of Engineering, the Chief Architect, and the team's engineers. You work closely with the Sr. Director while it is drafted. The Sr. Director owns how the work gets done (technical approach, standards, assignment, and quality), and you own priority. Expect the Sr. Director and others more senior than you to challenge your ranking. You are expected to defend it with evidence and make adjustments when a stronger case is made.

The role needs hands-on DevOps knowledge. You cannot specify a pipeline change, a cluster upgrade, a secrets rotation, or a new set of guardrails without understanding what each one puts at risk.

We use AI throughout our work and want you to find uses for it we have not thought of. We also expect you to do this job well if it were switched off tomorrow, because the priority calls and the stakeholder relationships depend on you.

This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports.

Responsibilities

* Own the intake path into the DevSecOps team, and qualify every request at the point of arrival: the desired outcome, affected parties, impact, dependencies, and any hard due dates. Where a request specifies its own solution, establish the problem it is meant to solve before the team commits to that solution.
* Rank inbound requests and Platform Engineering roadmap items on one backlog by urgency and value, publish the ranking, and keep it refined far enough ahead that an engineer can start without waiting on you for clarification. Make the trade-offs explicit, and answer to the teams whose work a ranking displaces. A stakeholder should be able to see what their request is weighed against and where it sits without escalating.
* Bring the team's improvement ideas to the Sr. Director as roadmap proposals, with the problem, scope, and effort worked out with the team's engineers and architects.
* Turn the Platform Engineering roadmap, including the IDP build-out, into backlog items the team can deliver, and keep their status current and published for the teams that depend on them. Report IDP adoption and user feedback to the Sr. Director.
* Limit work in progress to what the team can finish, resist mid-sprint insertion, and make the cost of an interruption visible when one is unavoidable.
* Translate requesters' needs into concrete platform, automation, tooling, and security requirements, written as stories with testable acceptance criteria that cover the impact of a failed change, rollback, access control, auditability, and cost alongside the functional outcome.
* Own the intake of unplanned and obligation-driven demand, including post-incident remediation and work generated by compliance, audit, and customer security commitments, and sequence it against everything else.
* Coordinate dependencies across internal teams and third-party vendors, and surface them early enough that they do not stall the queue.
* Report on flow: request-to-delivery lead time, work in progress, throughput, queue depth, the proportion of unplanned work, and the split between inbound requests and platform initiatives. Use the numbers to argue for more capacity or more automation.

Required skills & experience

* 2+ years as a Product Owner, Technical Product Owner, or in an equivalent backlog-owning role.
* 5+ years in DevOps, security operations, platform engineering, or site reliability engineering, with working experience in each of the following areas, using these or comparable tools:
  + Version control: Git
  + CI/CD: CircleCI, GitLab CI/CD, GitHub Actions
  + Cloud platforms: AWS, Google Cloud
  + Containers and orchestration: Docker, Kubernetes
  + Infrastructure as code: Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible
  + Scripting: Python, Bash, JavaScript
  + Monitoring and observability: Datadog, AppDynamics, CloudWatch, Splunk
  + Operating systems: Linux, UNIX
* Working knowledge of security practice for cloud infrastructure and delivery pipelines, including access control, secrets handling, and pipeline guardrails.
* Able to run an intake conversation with an engineer and come out of it with a complete requirement. Knows enough to spot what the engineer left out and what the change touches downstream.
* Writes acceptance criteria that account for adjacent systems, integrations, and existing platform behavior as well as the story itself.
* Translates business requirements into language a technical audience can act on, and technical constraints into terms a business stakeholder can decide against.
* Has ranked infrastructure or platform work against visible feature or customer work, and defended the ranking to stakeholders.
* Negotiation and conflict resolution: Has declined a request from a senior stakeholder, explained the reasoning, and kept the relationship intact.
* Has coordinated dependencies across multiple internal teams and external parties, and run a dependency tracker that the other teams on the program used.

Preferred skills & experience

* Point of sale experience.
* Has worked in a shared services or internal platform team serving internal customers with competing priorities, and can describe how the queue was managed.
* Has been on call, and knows from experience what unplanned work does to a team's ability to deliver.
* DevSecOps principles, such as shifting security left and zero trust.
* Platform engineering and GitOps: internal developer and monitoring platforms, self-service infrastructure, declarative deployment.
* Reliability and resilience practice such as chaos engineering, penetration testing requirements, and disaster-recovery drills. FinOps awareness for cloud cost accountability.
* AI and AIOps fluency, across both the platform (AI-assisted automation, predictive monitoring, self-healing pipelines) and the backlog (story generation, acceptance criteria drafting, requirements traceability).
* Has implemented an operational improvement in a past role that measurably improved the speed or quality of a delivery team's work, and can describe the change and its measured effect.
* Certifications such as AWS, Google, or Microsoft DevOps credentials.

Why OneView

Alongside the global retailers we already serve, we have recently been selected by one of the largest store networks in the world to replace their legacy store system, and are pursuing more retailers that have decided to replace theirs. The platform this role sets priorities for runs all of that work.

Our teams operate independently and set their own direction. Nobody needs a committee's permission to fix something that is broken. We expect people to identify what should be done differently and then make the change.

If you have worked in a larger organization where improvements you could see never got approved, this role is different: you work with the DevSecOps team's engineers and architects to propose their improvements, and you decide where approved work ranks.

OneView has been named one of Built In's *Best Places to Work* for three years in a row. Our leadership team brings decades of experience across software development, delivery, sales, and marketing.

*Applicants must have current, ongoing right to work in the UK (if applicable). OVC is not a licensed visa sponsor and is unable to sponsor a Skilled Worker visa or any other employment visa for this or any role, now or in the future. Evidence of right to work will be required prior to any offer of employment.*

You'll build to prove an idea with working prototypes, then work with our engineering team to take it into production.

Think startup within a startup: high agency, high visibility, very little bureaucracy and lots of room to grow.

**What you'll do**

This is a hands-on product role - as much about deciding what to build as building it. You'll work across product thinking, prototyping, engineering, AI, UX and deployment rather than owning one narrow part of the stack.

Current Open Agentic product areas include:

* Global Product Graph, our structured intelligence layer for insurance products.

We don't expect these to be the only things you'll work on. Part of the role is helping us discover and build what comes next.

* Take ambiguous product ideas and turn them into working software.
* Decide what to build now, what to defer and what not to build at all.
* Ship quickly, get things in front of real users and iterate on what you learn.
* Own products beyond the prototype - from zero to one, then from one to 100.
* Talk to customers and partners to find the problem worth solving, not just to validate a solution.

* Develop the insurance intelligence on top of it: product scoring, compliance evaluations, and what "good" means for a regulated AI deployment.
* Help shape both what Open Agentic builds and how we build it.

Within your first three months, we'd like you to have taken meaningful ownership of an AI-native product and shipped it. Within six months, to be owning a major product or workstream end-to-end and taking it towards real customer adoption and revenue.

**Who we're looking for**

We're looking for builders - people who get excited by a blank page, move quickly and naturally take ownership when something needs doing.

You'll probably have an engineering or computer science background and be able to build things yourself, but your ambitions sit in product: more interested in whether we're building the right thing than in owning the system that runs it.

You're probably more excited by the product and commercial applications than by perfecting the engineering, and you want the next few years to grow your product and commercial mind rather than your engineering craft.

**You can build.** You should be able to show us something you've personally built and deployed - we don't care whether it has 1 user (you) or 10 million - and explain how it works and the trade-offs you accepted. We're not asking you to own production systems. We are asking that you can prove an idea without needing a team.

**You have product judgment.** You start from the problem and who has it, not the feature. You're opinionated about what to build, comfortable arguing for what to leave out, and you can say how you'd know whether it worked. You notice when something feels bad - good UX, design and clear communication matter to you alongside good engineering - and you care whether people actually use the thing, not only whether the

**You're AI-native.** AI isn't something you recently added to your workflow because everyone else is talking about it - it's already fundamentally changed the way you build. You're deeply comfortable with tools such as Claude Code, the latest coding models, agentic development workflows and platforms such as Vercel, and you have opinions about which are good at what. You've also built *with* models rather than just alongside them, and know where they're reliable and where they aren't. You keep up with new models and research because you find the space genuinely exciting, and you have a view on where it's going.

**You have high agency.** You don't need a perfectly written PRD, detailed Jira tickets and three meetings before you can start. You're comfortable with: *"Here's the problem. Go figure out what we should build."*

**Staff Scientist – Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Theory**

At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it. Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve successfully transitioned quantum computing from an academic dream into a commercial reality. The most exciting thing is that we’re just getting started and we’ve recently closed our £260 million Series C funding round – the largest fundraise ever completed by a quantum computing company in Europe.

**The Purpose**

As a Staff Scientist specialising in Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Theory, you'll help shape OQC's path towards fault-tolerant quantum computing. You'll develop hardware-aware error correction strategies that combine the unique capabilities of our multimode superconducting processors with advanced codes, decoders and fault-tolerant protocols, turning theoretical breakthroughs into practical advances in quantum hardware.

**The Role**

Joining our Quantum Error Correction research team, you'll be a recognised technical authority, helping define the scientific direction of OQC's error correction strategy.

You'll work at the intersection of quantum information theory and experimental hardware, developing QEC approaches for our next-generation OQC GENESIS platform and Dimon architecture. By combining erasure detection within individual devices with error correction across multiple encoded qubits, you'll tackle some of the most important challenges on the path to scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing.

This is a senior individual contributor role with significant scientific autonomy and influence. You'll take ownership of ambitious research projects, collaborate closely with experimentalists and engineers, mentor fellow scientists and help translate cutting-edge research into the technical requirements that shape OQC's future processors.

**What You'll Be Working On**

* Develop and benchmark hardware-aware QEC schemes that combine error detection within OQC's multimode devices with error correction across encoded qubit arrays.
* Design advanced quantum codes and decoders that exploit syndrome measurements and erasure information while accounting for imperfect detection and residual errors.
* Build and validate circuit-level noise models alongside experimental teams, incorporating relaxation, dephasing, leakage, crosstalk and correlated errors.
* Optimise syndrome extraction, erasure-check schedules and fault-tolerant protocols around hardware connectivity, native operations, measurement times and decoding constraints.
* Evaluate logical memories and operations, balancing logical error rates, physical qubit overheads, execution time and classical decoding costs.
* Translate theoretical findings into quantitative hardware, control and readout requirements, collaborating with experimentalists to design and validate critical experiments.
* Lead complex scientific investigations, develop reproducible simulation and analysis tools, mentor colleagues and communicate research through publications, conferences and technical collaborations.

**What We're Looking For**

* A PhD in Quantum Information, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science or a related discipline, or an equivalent record of significant research experience.
* A strong track record of original contributions to quantum error correction, fault-tolerant quantum computing or related quantum information research, demonstrated through publications, research software or other substantive outputs.
* Deep understanding of quantum information theory, including stabiliser formalism, quantum noise channels and fault-tolerance principles.
* Expertise in topological codes, including surface or colour codes, or quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes.
* Experience with decoding methods for erasure and Pauli noise, including matching-based approaches, belief propagation or ordered-statistics decoding.
* Strong understanding of fault-tolerant logical operations, such as lattice surgery, code switching, transversal gates or magic-state preparation and distillation.
* Experience with circuit-level simulation, logical error-rate estimation and resource analysis informed by experimental data.
* Strong scientific programming skills in Python or C++, particularly for simulation, decoder implementation and reproducible research.
* Proven ability to independently lead scientific investigations, combine analytical and numerical approaches, and translate theoretical findings into practical hardware insights.
* Excellent scientific communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence research direction and work effectively across theoretical and experimental disciplines.

**The 'Nice-to-Haves'**

* Experience with erasure-aware QEC, dual-rail encodings or concatenated error correction schemes combining inner error detection with outer error correction.
* Knowledge of superconducting quantum circuits, particularly multimode transmons and their application to quantum error correction.

Palo Alto Networks (Idira) is looking for a Domain Consultant/Senior Solutions Engineer covering the UK&I region.

**About The Role:**

We're looking for a Lead/Head of Transaction Monitoring (Enterprise) to own how Paysend detects suspicious activity across all products, corridors and payment methods, and to lead the TM Enterprise Program that modernises it.

**Objective and Key Results**

**Objective (Q4 2026):** AI-Powered Enterprise Financial Crime: build scalable, risk-based transaction monitoring

Enterprise clients can submit legitimate transactions with minimal friction, suspicious transactions are correctly identified and declined, unnecessary RFIs are minimised, and transaction-monitoring performance is measurable and continuously optimised.

Metrics clearly separate client-generated risk, Financial Crime controls and downstream payout execution, so TM declines are not confused with prefunding, network or technical failures, and stages reconcile without double-counting.

**Key Results you will be accountable for**

* **% Confirmed Fraud Rate of Enterprise-Initiated Transactions:** Confirmed fraud transactions divided by total enterprise-initiated transactions, broken down by client, typology, transaction type and destination, and confirmed vs. suspected fraud. Gives clients an evidence-based view of the quality of the volume they submit.
* **% Legitimate Transaction Straight-Through Processing Rate:** Legitimate transactions processed without an RFI divided by total legitimate transactions submitted. The central measure of balance between risk protection and customer friction.
* **% Enterprise TM Decision Quality:** Combines confirmed-fraud prevention rate (stopped before payout), false-positive rate, and control coverage of material enterprise TM risks by documented, approved and tested controls.
* **% Enterprise TM Investigation Efficiency:** Median RFI time to resolution, % resolved within SLA, % with a clear documented decision, % outstanding beyond SLA, and RFI backlog and ageing.

**What you will own**

job_title: Bath Engineering & Design Studentships: Foundation Reuse for Net-Zero Construction
job_description:
## Description

*This project is one of a number in competition for a studentship from the Faculty of Engineering and Design at the University of Bath.*

*If successful, this studentship is expected to commence 04 October 2027.*

*An alternative start date may be possible if agreed with your intended supervisors and the Doctoral College.*

The construction industry faces increasing pressure to reduce embodied carbon and transition towards more circular use of materials and infrastructure. Reusing existing foundations, rather than automatically replacing them during redevelopment, offers substantial potential to reduce concrete consumption, construction waste, cost and programme. However, widespread adoption is limited by uncertainty regarding the condition, geometry, capacity and future performance of ageing foundations.

This project will develop new approaches for assessing the suitability of existing foundations for reuse. The research will combine probabilistic methods, enhanced analytical and numerical modelling, monitoring data and non-destructive testing to quantify uncertainty in existing foundation performance and support rational reuse decisions.

Key research questions will include how ageing, consolidation, pore-pressure changes and deterioration affect foundation performance; how existing foundation capacity can be inferred from limited historical records and in-situ testing; how uncertainty can be incorporated within reliability-based assessment; and how sufficient confidence can be demonstrated for safe, code-compliant reuse. The project will also investigate how additional testing and monitoring can reduce uncertainty and inform decisions on whether an existing foundation can be reused, strengthened or requires replacement.

The overall aim is to establish a practical framework for making safe and confident engineering decisions under sparse and uncertain data conditions, helping move foundation reuse from occasional engineering practice towards a more systematic component of low-carbon construction.

## Entry Requirements

Applicants must have, or be about to obtain, a UK Honours degree 1st or 2.1, or international equivalent. A master’s level qualification would also be advantageous.

**Non-UK applicants, who are not currently studying in the UK, must meet the programme’s** English language requirement **before the application deadline – no exceptions will be considered.**

Applicants should have a strong background in civil, structural or geotechnical engineering, or a closely related discipline. Experience or interest in geotechnical engineering, foundation behaviour, numerical modelling, probabilistic methods or structural reliability would be advantageous.

## Fees

Applicants will be considered for a studentship. Studentships cover tuition fees, provide a £1k per annum training support fee, and a maintenance stipend (£21,805 2026/27 rate). International students will be required to cover the cost of a Student visa and Immigration Health Surcharge from personal funds.

## How To Apply

Informal enquiries are encouraged. Direct these to Dr Cormac Reale - cr760@bath.ac.uk

Please follow the below instructions carefully.

You must make a formal application via the University of Bath’s online application form for a **PhD in Civil Engineering**

**Please note that you can apply for a maximum of two PhD projects on this programme.**

In the ‘Funding Your Studies’ section, you must select ‘University of Bath URSA’ from one of the drop-down menus.

In the ‘Your PhD project’ section, you must quote the project title in the PhD project title field, and you must quote the lead supervisor’s name in the field ‘Name of intended supervisor at University of Bath.’

If you are applying for two projects, you must quote the project title for your second choice project in the field ‘Project 2 Title’ and the lead supervisor’s name in ‘Name of intended supervisor for 2nd choice project at University of Bath.

**You must ensure that you follow the above steps correctly. Failure to complete these steps will cause errors in the automated processing of your application and may mean that you are not considered for a particular project.**

job_title: Bath Engineering & Design Studentships: Systems modelling for sustainable battery recycling
job_description:
*This project is one of a number in competition for a studentship from the Faculty of Engineering and Design at the University of Bath. If successful, this studentship is expected to commence 04 October 2027.*

*An alternative start date may be possible if agreed with your intended supervisors and the Doctoral College.*

The lead supervisor for this project will be Dr Evangelos Kallitsis, who will join the University of Bath before the project start date.

The rapid transition to electric mobility is shifting reliance from fossil fuels to mineral resources. Central to this transition are lithium-ion batteries, with a large volume expected to reach end of life over the coming decades. Sustainably managing these end-of-life flows requires recycling processes that are scalable, profitable and environmentally beneficial. In principle, recycling displaces mined materials such as lithium and cobalt and reduces environmental impacts at product level [1], and recent industrial-scale data suggest it outperforms mining supply chains [2]. However, these benefits depend strongly on battery chemistry and process configuration, and the feed to recycling plants is changing. Today's end-of-life stream is dominated by nickel- and cobalt-rich NMC cells and manufacturing scrap, but it will increasingly contain lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion cells with far lower metal value [3]. Plants designed now will operate for decades, yet process models and life cycle assessments (LCAs) typically evaluate one route for one fixed feed. Dynamic models are needed that can assess, and design for, this changing technological landscape. 

This PhD will develop a systems modelling framework for designing battery recycling processes under changing economic, technological and regulatory conditions, by:

- Performing dynamic material flow analysis (MFA) to forecast the volume and composition of end-of-life battery flows reaching recycling plants to 2050.

- Developing a superstructure of flowsheet options (pyrometallurgical, hydrometallurgical and direct recycling) and performing targeted process simulation to generate mass and energy balances.

# Manufacturing Material Accuracy Analyst

Job Summary

The Manufacturing Material Accuracy Analyst improves the accuracy of materials used to build Prestige homes, lodges and buildings. The role compares approved bills of materials (BOMs) with what is issued, consumed, returned and recorded against each build, then reconciles those records to physical stock. Working with Production, Technical, Procurement, Stores, Finance and Internal Logistics, the analyst identifies the causes and value of discrepancies, secures approved corrections and prevents repeat losses. Reliable material information supports build quality, delivery, stock availability and margin.

Accountabilities

Material usage and BOM integrity

•  Compare approved BOM quantities and specifications with actual material use by build, model and product family, including customer options and design revisions where applicable.

•  Establish a clear audit trail for material issues, returns, substitutions, rework, scrap, offcuts and other non-standard use, distinguishing valid build variation from loss or recording error.

•  Highlight inaccurate quantities, units of measure, item codes and specifications; agree proposed BOM or master-data changes with the authorised Technical and system owners before implementation.

•  Check that approved engineering changes and product introductions are reflected in the correct BOM version and effective date before drawing conclusions from a variance.

Stock and transaction accuracy

•  Reconcile materials issued and consumed in the ERP/MRP system with production records and physical stock, investigating gaps between the three sources.

•  Review timing and completeness of booking, stock transfers, returns, scrap declarations, substitutions and adjustments; work with process owners to correct transactions at source.

•  Support targeted cycle counts and stock checks on high-value or high-variance materials, documenting count differences and the evidence behind any recommended adjustment.

•  Identify process or data weaknesses that cause shortages, duplicated issues, incorrect costs or distorted work-in-progress and stock balances.

Variance investigation and corrective action

•  Prioritise discrepancies by quantity, financial value, recurrence and risk to production, quality or customer delivery.

•  Investigate root causes with the people closest to the work, including BOM error, incorrect picking, unrecorded use, damage, waste, theft risk, supplier short delivery or transaction timing; record evidence before assigning a cause.

•  Agree corrective actions with accountable owners, track completion and test whether the change reduces repeat variance.

•  Escalate material losses, suspected control failures and unresolved high-value differences promptly through the Head of Internal Logistics and relevant functional leaders.

Reporting and continuous improvement

•  Maintain clear, repeatable reports on BOM-to-actual variance, physical-to-system stock accuracy, scrap, adjustments and write-offs, with trends by material and product family.

•  Present both quantity and cost impact, explain significant movements and distinguish confirmed savings from estimates.

•  Recommend practical changes to material presentation, issue and return processes, data controls and shop-floor recording; help teams implement approved improvements.

•  Support periodic reviews with Production, Technical, Procurement, Stores and Finance to agree priorities, resolve ownership and close aged issues.

Health and safety, quality and inclusion

•  Follow site health and safety procedures when observing production or checking stock, and report hazards and unsafe practices.

•  Escalate any material discrepancy that may affect product specification, traceability or customer quality; do not authorise unapproved substitutions.

•  Work respectfully with colleagues across all departments and uphold company equality and diversity standards.

Key Measures of Success

•  A sustained reduction in BOM-to-actual consumption variance, measured in quantity and value.

•  Improved physical-to-system stock accuracy for the materials reviewed.

•  Fewer unexplained adjustments and material write-offs, with improved visibility of the causes of loss.

•  Timely closure and verified effectiveness of agreed corrective actions.

You'll own the **enterprise AI harness around Spark: the layer that lets an enterprise put agents to work at scale and trust them with more over time**. Permissioning, audit, and limits so agents act within the organization's policies. Bring-your-own-model and model routing so every task runs on the right model at the right cost. Agentic automation so agents run on triggers and schedules across a product organization, not only when asked. And the control plane that lets a customer see every agent running, what it costs, how well it performs, and how far it's allowed to go on its own. You'll spend real time with enterprise customers, translate what they need into product, and make sure they get value at scale with the governance they require. The rules for how agents operate inside a company are being written right now, and you'll write them into the product. Our customers are product organizations inside large companies. **Job Overview**

Qualcomm is looking for an experienced **CPU Physical Design Integration Engineer** to join the **Nuvia Data Center CPU team in Cambridge, UK**. This team is focused on developing next-generation, high-performance, and power-efficient custom CPU technologies for advanced compute and server platforms, driving innovation across the industry.

In this position, you will play a key role in the physical design, integration, and verification of high-frequency CPU designs. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional teams, including microarchitecture, RTL design, CAD, circuit design, block-level physical design, and SoC-level physical design, to deliver production-ready designs.

Your responsibilities will span the full CPU physical design flow, including synthesis, floorplanning, partitioning, power planning, IP integration, clock and power distribution, reliability analysis, power and noise analysis, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, and electrical rule checking.

This role offers the opportunity to impact CPU architecture and design methodologies from early planning stages through implementation, signoff, and silicon validation.

The position is offered at the **Staff Engineer** level, with responsibilities, ownership, and technical leadership commensurate with your experience.

**Key Responsibilities will include**

As a **Server CPU Physical Design Integration Engineer**, you will:

* Own Final CPU Layout database Implementation, Integration and Verification of high frequency next-generation data center CPU designs.
* Driving block partitioning, floorplan implementation and pin placement strategies.
* Work with SOC team and other IP teams to ensure all technical, interface and integration requirements are met.
* Partner with CAD and physical design teams to develop and improve flows for chip-level integration, validation and analysis.
* Working collaboratively with project team members to identify and resolve issues which arise during the design cycle and take the key learnings into the next product cycle.
* For Staff-level candidates, provide technical leadership, mentor engineers, influence cross-functional methodology, and drive resolution of complex and critical Integration challenges.

**Required Skills and Experience**

We are seeking candidates with strong experience in **CPU physical design implementation Domain,** preferably with experience delivering complex, high-performance CPU designs.

The ideal candidate will have:

* Deep CPU-specific expertise across multiple areas of structural and physical design, including synthesis, timing closure, multi-power-domain analysis, structured placement and routing.
* Experience collaborating closely with leading EDA vendors to develop, enhance, and optimize tool capabilities for designing high-speed, low-power, synthesizable CPU cores.
* Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area.
* Hands-on involvement in developing, refining, and automating physical design methodologies and implementation flows.
* Strong leadership and communication skills with the ability to work effectively with global, cross-functional distributed teams across architecture, RTL, CAD, circuit design, physical design, SoC, and verification disciplines.
* Proficiency in scripting and automation to improve productivity, debug efficiency, and design-flow scalability, including the adoption of GenAI-driven initiatives where applicable.
* Scripting to automate tasks and improve debug efficiency including genAI initiatives.
* Experience working with industry-standard EDA implementation and signoff flows for physical design, timing analysis, power analysis, and physical verification.

**Minimum Qualifications**

Candidates should typically have one of the following:

* Bachelor’s degree in **Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science**, or a related technical field with relevant experience in hardware engineering, CPU design, physical design, clock design, or implementation.

**OR**

* Master’s degree in **Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science**, or a related technical field with relevant experience in hardware engineering, CPU design, physical design, clock design, or implementation.

**OR**

* PhD in **Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science**, or a related technical field with relevant experience in CPU design, physical implementation, clock design, or circuit-aware methodology.

The role is intended for experienced candidates and is open for **Staff Engineer** level.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Experience in any of the following areas would be highly valuable:

* Experience leading or contributing to **CPU, GPU, or large SoC physical design integration** from early floorplanning through final GDS tapeout.
* Strong background in top-level or chip-level physical design, including floorplanning, partitioning, pin placement, power planning, clock distribution, IP integration, and final layout database assembly.
* Hands-on experience **with hierarchical physical design methodologies**, including top-down planning, budgeting, block integration, timing convergence, and physical convergence.
* Experience working with **advanced semiconductor process nodes,** especially 7nm and below.
* Strong understanding of **place and route**, clock tree synthesis, structured placement, routing optimization, congestion analysis, and design closure methodologies.
* Familiarity with **power-aware implementation techniques**, including multi-voltage domains, power gating, clock gating, IR drop mitigation, EM analysis, and power integrity closure.
* Experience integrating **hard IP, memory macros, mixed-signal blocks, PLLs, clocking structures, and third-party IP** into large-scale CPU or SoC designs.
* Ability to analyse implementation and signoff results, identify design bottlenecks, and drive improvements **in power, performance, area, reliability, and manufacturability.**
* Experience developing automation or analysis flows using **TCL, Python, Perl**, or similar scripting languages.
* For Staff-level candidates, demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives, influence cross-functional teams, define methodology, and mentor other engineers.

**What We Value**

We are especially interested in engineers who:

* Have strong fundamentals in **physical design, timing, power, routing, clocking, and layout verification**.
* Enjoy solving complex integration challenges across **floorplanning, partitioning, power planning, clock distribution, timing closure, physical verification, and tapeout readiness**.
* Bring a structured, analytical, and data-driven approach to debug, convergence, signoff closure, and methodology improvement.
* Communicate clearly and effectively across microarchitecture, RTL, circuit design, CAD, timing, SoC integration, IP, and physical design teams.
* Are proactive in identifying risks, driving cross-functional issue resolution, and capturing learnings to improve future product cycles.
* Show technical curiosity and a continuous-improvement mindset, including the ability to automate repetitive tasks and improve debug efficiency.
* Can provide technical leadership while remaining hands-on in complex design closure and integration challenges.
* Thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced engineering environment where technical depth, execution quality, and cross-team partnership are essential.

**Benefits and Perks**

At Qualcomm, you will be part of a collaborative engineering culture focused on innovation, technical excellence, and meaningful product impact.

We offer:

* Competitive compensation package, including base salary, performance-related bonus, and equity opportunities.
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan and equity programs supporting employee share ownership and long-term participation in Qualcomm’s success.
* Pension and retirement support, including a matching pension scheme.
* Health and wellbeing benefits, including medical, life, income protection, and wellbeing resources.
* Maternity, paternity, family, and extended leave support to help employees balance professional and personal commitments.
* Education assistance and tuition support to enable continued learning and professional development.
* Relocation and immigration support where applicable, particularly for strong candidates moving to join the Cambridge team.
* Employee assistance and resilience programs supporting mental wellbeing, balance, and personal resilience.
* Opportunities to connect through employee networks, community programs, volunteering, and social groups that support inclusion, collaboration, and community engagement.
* Subsidised wellbeing and lifestyle benefits, which may include gym or fitness support, bicycle purchase schemes, and employee clubs.
* A flexible, collaborative, and technically challenging work environment, with the opportunity to work alongside highly skilled engineers on advanced CPU technology.

**Why Join the Nuvia Data Center CPU Team in Cambridge?**

 Cambridge is Qualcomm’s largest office in the UK, with approximately 400 team members across engineering, business strategy, and support functions. From an engineering perspective, the Cambridge site includes teams focused on RF and PMU analog design, digital design and verification, digital physical design, embedded software, packaging, and post-silicon validation. Target products include high-performance CPUs and GPUs, ultra-low-power IoT devices, and wearables such as smart glasses, smart watches, and earbuds.

The Nuvia Data Center CPU team is building advanced custom CPU technology for next-generation compute platforms. As a **CPU Physical Design Integration Engineer**, you will play a key role in taking complex CPU designs from Implementation through integration, verification and final tapeout readiness.

This role offers the opportunity to work on challenging aspects of CPU physical design integration, including floorplanning, partitioning, IP integration, power and clock distribution, timing convergence, physical verification, power integrity, and final layout database assembly. You will collaborate closely with architecture, RTL, CAD, circuit design, block-level physical design, SoC, and signoff teams to deliver high-frequency, power-efficient, manufacturable CPU products.

This is an opportunity to contribute to technically demanding data center CPU designs, influence physical design methodology across future product generations, and make a direct impact on world-class silicon products developed by a highly experienced engineering team in Cambridge.

• Bachelor's degree in Science, Engineering, or related field and 4+ years of ASIC design, verification, validation, integration, or related work experience.  
 OR  
Master's degree in Science, Engineering, or related field and 3+ years of ASIC design, verification, validation, integration, or related work experience.  
 OR  
PhD in Science, Engineering, or related field and 2+ years of ASIC design, verification, validation, integration, or related work experience.

### **Roku is changing how the world watches TV**

Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

### What does the team work on?

The Ads Customer Interfaces team develops full-stack web application services, APIs, and UIs that provide a unified approach to interfacing with internal and external customers across Roku's suite of advertising products. Our mission is to provide the best-in-class user experience and service while aiming to delight users of our products by making their jobs easier and allowing them to focus on their customers instead of getting bogged down by tedious business processes. In this role, you will work as a key member of the Ads Customer Interfaces team.

### What is the role?

Roku pioneered streaming to the TV and continues to innovate and lead the industry. While we are well-positioned to help shape the future of television and streaming media worldwide, continued success stems from experienced software engineers like you developing core features for the Roku platform.

Our new Senior Software Engineer will be contributing extensively to our container orchestrated platform, bringing together some of the latest web technologies with Ai expertise to develop a truly scalable and responsive web applications. To be successful you’ll need extensive experience of building reliable and scalable cloud-based solutions, a strong background in software engineering and an appetite to keep on top of modern software practices. This is a great role for a senior professional who enjoys a high level of visibility and thrives on great business impact.

The features and performance improvements you implement directly impact millions of users every day. This is a great role for an experienced professional who has innovative ideas for complex problems and can translate these ideas into ultra-reliable software.

### How will I use AI at Roku?

At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact.

We value your AI skills if have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.

### What are the responsiblities of the role?

* Design, develop and deliver high-quality web applications and back-end services with modern frameworks and technologies.
* Work as a part of a high functioning team consisting of UX designers, software engineers, dev-ops, quality assurance and product management.
* Build and integrate AI-powered features into web applications and enterprise tools.
* Build and optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) solutions to power chatbot interactions
* Work both independently and paired with other team members to ensure efficient delivery of prioritised features.
* Take part in the planning and refinement of features along with the team to come up with innovative and collaborative designs.
* Develop new features and write test cases to ensure the quality of your code.
* Work with CI/CD tools to ensure that all software developed adheres to both quality and scaling requirements.
* Take a role in continuously improving our software delivery process, making it as efficient as possible, reducing wasteful activities and creating value.
* See a feature go all the way from design stage to being deployed into customer facing environments.
* Demonstrate the ability to dig deep to find solutions to challenging problems affecting our users.

### What experience would help someone be successful in this role at Roku?

* Extensive expeirence  in JavaScript/TypeScript and modern web frameworks (React, Next.js, Angular, Node.js, Express) on cloud-based technology, such as AWS and GCP.
* Experience of building large scale and low latency distributed systems.
* Solid understanding of algorithms, data structures, performance optimisation techniques, object-oriented programming.
* Experience using modern AI-assisted and agentic development workflows in day-to-day engineering using AI/ML APIs and SDKs
* Hands-on experience developing RAG solutions or working with LLMs for chatbots is preferred
* In-depth understanding of CI/CD and the tools used to implement them, such as Jenkins.
* Experience with software repository tools, such as GitLab and GitHub.
* Experience with productivity tools, such as Jira and Confluence.
* A good understanding of Agile practices.
* Ability to accurately estimate software tasks and work to schedule.
* Exposure to observability tools and practices (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana) are preferred.

* Track record of tuning performance and reliability for highly available services and web applications

* Bachelors of Masters Degree in Compute Science/Software Engineering or related subject

* Experience designing data contracts with Engineering, covering schema, semantics, ownership and freshness.

# Verification & Validation (V&V) Discipline Lead

**We're building the UK's next generation engineering powerhouse, providing critical technology that strengthens national security and resilience.**

We specialise in turning advances in sensing, AI, and communications into operational capability for the edge, where connectivity may be degraded or denied. Our work focuses on accelerating the deployment of technology, improving decision-making for frontline teams, and protecting people and critical assets in demanding environments.

Headquartered in Bristol, Rowden employs around 200 people and operates over 20,000 square feet of engineering and manufacturing facilities. We have a growing international footprint and are one of Europe's fastest-growing engineering businesses.

**About the role**

Rowden already has an excellent systems engineering team, and we already integrate, test and verify complex edge systems. However, the scale, pace and complexity of what we need to prove is changing, and with it our demand for a rigorous, end-to-end verification & validation (V&V) capability.

Our systems bring together software, compute, networks, radios, sensors, user devices and increasingly autonomous behaviour. They have to work across denied, degraded, intermittent and low bandwidth networks, where system behaviour shifts as connectivity and available resources shift. Right now, too much of our evidence that a system works comes from late, bespoke, one-off test campaigns rather than a coherent V&V strategy applied from the start. It is often manual and hard to reuse, which slows everyone down and leaves gaps between what we've proven and what we've assumed.

So, we are investing properly in V&V, and we're looking for the person to own it. V&V is the broader discipline: deciding, for every requirement and every stakeholder need, what evidence is needed and how best to get it, whether that's test, analysis, inspection, demonstration, modelling or simulation. System Integration & Test (SI&T) is one of the most important execution capabilities within that discipline, and will sit within your remit: building the reusable test and evaluation infrastructure, integrating real systems, and proving they work under realistic conditions. The goal is a world-leading V&V capability for edge information systems, built on reusable methods and infrastructure rather than one-off rigs, so we can verify and validate earlier, far more often, and with evidence we can trust.

Executed well, this will significantly speed up the time it takes to get technology into users' hands - and give us confidence it will actually work for them when it gets there.

You need to understand verification and validation deeply enough to know what good looks like across the full range of methods, not just testing, and be excited about designing and evolving a capability, rather than only operating a process. You will also stay close to the work - expect to be technically hands-on, working alongside teams rather than only directing them.

**We're building the UK's next generation engineering powerhouse, providing critical technology that strengthens national security and resilience.**

We specialise in turning advances in sensing, AI, and communications into operational capability for the edge, where connectivity may be degraded or denied. Few product roles offer the opportunity to work across all four. You will own an increasingly important product domain for our EMEA business, shaping how consent capabilities develop alongside our advertising, data and measurement products and working with regional and global product, engineering and privacy teams to make it happen.  
  
This is a role for someone who enjoys navigating technical complexity, influencing across global teams and building product capabilities that sit at the foundation of a growing advertising and services business.  
  
We are expanding our Product & Go-To-Market function and looking for a Privacy Product Lead to join our rapidly growing advertising and services business, on an on-going contract basis.   
  
The Privacy Product Lead is the product owner for consent and privacy-related products in EMEA. This role owns the product roadmap, requirements and delivery sequencing for our consent capabilities, including the management and development of existing consent mechanisms.  
  
The role works closely with our data and privacy compliance function to translate legal and regulatory requirements into clear product requirements, and with global product and engineering teams to ensure those requirements are understood, prioritised and delivered.  
  
This is not a privacy or legal role. Privacy owns regulatory interpretation, policy and compliance. This role owns the product: what needs to be built, how it is prioritised and how it gets delivered.

**Role and Responsibilities**

**Your key responsibilities**

  

Consent & Privacy Product Ownership

·        Own the EMEA product roadmap for consent and privacy-related products, including our existing consent mechanisms. Set the strategy and priorities for the domain, define what needs to be built or changed, and maintain clear product ownership through delivery and ongoing operation.

·        Work closely with the Ad Experiences and Data & Measurement Product & GTM teams to understand their requirements and ensure the consent and privacy product roadmap supports the products and capabilities they are developing.

Product Delivery & Technical Readiness

·        Translate the roadmap into clear product requirements and work with global product and engineering teams to get them delivered. Own requirements, acceptance criteria, delivery sequencing and testing, manage technical dependencies and risks, and ensure capabilities are ready for implementation and rollout.

Product & Privacy Partnership
