**About the role**

We are recruiting two Senior Programme Managers to join the UKRI Infrastructure Team and play key roles in supporting the delivery of the Next National Supercomputing Service (NNSS) and managing the National Compute Resource (NCR) portfolio. The NNSS and NCRs are cornerstone investments at the heart of the DSIT-UKRI compute roadmap published in July 2025. The NNSS is a £750 million strategic investment for the UK government, to ensure the UK research and innovation community continues to have access to the most advanced modelling and simulation capabilities. It will provide innovative compute hardware at the University of Edinburgh, alongside the services, software and support needed to enable researchers and innovators to make effective use of this national resource. The NCR portfolio comprises a range of smaller scale compute resources funded by UKRI that are designed to be diverse, user-centred, coherent and serving the needs of the UK.

These roles are within the Digital Research Infrastructure (DRI) pillar, which alongside the Infrastructure Fund and Portfolio pillars form the cross-cutting UKRI Infrastructure Team that coordinates and manages UKRI’s Infrastructure portfolio. You will collaborate across the organisation and externally, engaging with relevant collaborators in government departments, Public Sector Research Establishments (PSREs), academia and industry to gather insight and ensure that UKRI’s plans for compute infrastructure enable our varied communities to use the most powerful digital tools and techniques.

As a Senior Programme Manager, you will lead and take part in a wide range of strategic and operational activities that support the successful and effective delivery of the NNSS and NCR investments. These responsibilities will range from developing policy and managing stakeholders, to facilitating governance boards and working with service providers resolving operational system issues. As part of this role, you will work closely with colleagues across UKRI and engage regularly with peers and senior leaders, playing a key part in shaping the future of UK’s compute infrastructure landscape and ensuring that UKRI’s investments deliver maximum value for the research and innovation community. You will be working particularly closely with the Head of Service Delivery and the Head of Policy and Engagement of NNSS.

We encourage candidates with an interest and knowledge in large-scale compute and related aspects of DRI to apply for this position: relevant experience might have been gained from several different types of career path or educational background. It is likely that the successful candidate will have the opportunity to work for periods with other policy or technical teams within UKRI to enhance the knowledge needed for their work.

**Your responsibilities:**

* Support the development, delivery and operation of key investments in the UKRI national compute ecosystem, including the NNSS, the NNSS Grand Challenges initiatives, the NCRs and Community Centres of Excellence.
* Develop and implement the access and allocation policy for the compute services to ensure fair, open and appropriate distribution of compute resources for effective utilisation of the entire portfolio of compute investments.
* Maintain and develop project management processes to ensure successful delivery of the compute investments, including appropriate governance, monitoring, assurance and evaluation approaches.
* Build and cultivate strong relationships across a range of stakeholders including users in the research and innovation communities, service providers and colleagues internally and Government departments.
* Provide high-quality expertise and advice in your area of responsibility, informed by evidence and engagement with relevant partners.
* Represent the UKRI Infrastructure team in meetings with internal and external collaborators.
* Contribute to strategic projects across the Infrastructure team, as required.

* Support the DTC Lead to develop and refresh the overall strategy for Biotech and Health programmes.

# **Customer Success Manager**

A new, exciting opportunity to join Undo’s Customer Success team with a focus on learning and development. 

Undo is a fast-growing, exciting deep-tech company whose breakthrough technology is changing the way people develop software. The company is a small, intimate and highly-skilled team, and its products are used by many of the world’s most important technology companies. The technology is highly valuable but very complex, and is deployed in some of the world’s most complex software development environments. Customer retention and growth is excellent (net revenue retention of 125%) but careful management is required to achieve this success.

### Purpose of this role:

A Customer Success Manager is responsible for ensuring our strategic customers are delighted and successful using our products.

### Responsibilities:

* Establish and maintain strong and long-lasting technical relationships within major enterprise accounts.
* Drive a high level of customer satisfaction and customer retention through successful product use. (Daily/Weekly/Monthly and Net Active Users and session counts as the KPIs.)
* Create a success plan in partnership with your customer including onboarding, training, driving utilization, conducting routine business reviews, and orchestrating resources aligned to driving customer value.
* Comply with best practice operating strategies and provide ideas and feedback to improve and enhance these.
* Liaise with our technical team to support customers through the technical deployment phase all the way to quarterly reviews and annual renewals.
* Deliver against the defined OKRs.
* Translate insights from your customers into actionable tasks that can be shared with your team and peers, whilst supporting collaboration across departments to help drive change.
* Work closely with the Sales team to align on strategies, products, coverage plans, and account opportunities.
* Work closely with the Product/Engineering team to provide product feedback and help craft changes to the product to enhance customer satisfaction and accelerate adoption.
* Understand the customer journey, identify pain points and bottlenecks and find innovative ways to improve the customer’s overall experience.
* Demonstrate ROI to customers and establish metrics to advise them on best practice and optimisation of the products.
* Delivering training to end users and train the trainer programmes.
* Ensuring that we have achieved “awareness coverage” across accounts
* Note: This role will likely involve some overseas travel.

### Personal attributes:

At Undo, the way we work and interact is as important as our technical skills. The following personal attributes will be key to your success here:

* **Results-oriented**: You are focused on achieving tangible, agreed benefits, looking beyond just the completion of activities.
* **Customer-Focused**: You try to get a deep understanding of specific customer needs and use this to guide your decisions and actions. You can “energise” teams of  engineers and others who work on your accounts.
* **Reliable & Driven**: You demonstrate high energy, consistent focus, and a positive, productive attitude that contributes to team morale. You honour your commitments, actively seek to improve, and know when to seek assistance.
* **Team Player**: You support your colleagues and engage constructively in discussions, even with differing opinions, fostering a positive team environment.
* **Empathetic & Resilient**: You understand others’ viewpoints and maintain composure and a can-do attitude in challenging situations.
* **Solutions-Oriented**: You identify and analyze issues, anticipate outcomes, and clearly articulate a supporting vision with enthusiasm.
* **Aligned**: You proactively use company and team objectives to inform your work.

* Project management experience in industries related to Software / Technology.
* Previous customer-facing roles for example in sales engineering, sales support, professional services, field engineering, customer success or customer support.
* Ability to manage multiple stakeholders both inside the customer and inside Undo, and to achieve your goals through others over whom you have no direct authority.
* Enthusiastic and hungry to join a small and dynamic deep-tech company with great potential, help shape the customer success function and share ideas across the business to help drive growth.
* Experience building and maintaining relationships whilst working to mitigate churn and drive adoption and renewals.
* Comfortable in a start-up environment, we wear many hats and move quickly.

It is imperative that you are able to understand our products to allow you to meaningfully talk about them internally and with customers. Experience supporting software engineers as end users is a must. Past software development experience would be very helpful. This however is not a technical role: You will have direct access to a dedicated highly-skilled engineering team to achieve technical goals.

Permanent

Cambridge, UK (office-based or hybrid with at least 1-2 days per week in the office)

# Head of CRM - Premium Supplements Brand

## Own the channel that drives 80 to 90% of a fast-growing wellness brand’s revenue, £90-100k, near Brighton.

East Sussex (near Brighton), 4 days a week in the office  
£90,000 to £100,000

Retention drives 80 to 90% of UK revenue at this brand-first wellness business, and the UK is its biggest market. The job is to own the channel that pays for everything else.

The business is in high growth and expanding fast in the US. It’s past the scrappy startup stage but not yet corporate, and the systems are still being built while the expectations are already big-business. You’ll report into the Chief Digital Officer, with real visibility at founder and board level, and the room to run CRM your way.

**What you’ll own**

You’ll set CRM strategy across a database of roughly 700k. Most revenue comes from subscription, so this isn’t a “send more emails” job. The work is knowing how to treat prospects, customers and subscribers differently, how to move people between those groups, and when to leave subscribers alone. Upsell, cross-sell and lifetime value sit at the heart of it.

You’ll lead a team of five (a senior manager and four execs across the UK, US and Europe). You’ll also design what the team looks like next: where to split UK and international, flows and campaigns, and where to add headcount. Building people’s careers, through mentoring, succession planning and clear growth paths, is as big a part of the role as the numbers.

You’ll work closely with the customer experience lead, who owns the tech stack and subscription operations.

**Who you are**

* You’ve led CRM at a brand-first business. Beauty, skincare, fashion, wellness or jewellery would be great, but what matters is that you know how to make emails beautiful and take people on a journey, and you back it up with data.
* You’ve been through a real growth phase at a scale-up, and you know what structure, process and team design look like when a business is growing up fast.
* You’ve ideally led a loyalty programme. Subscription experience is a bonus, not a must, but you understand why LTV matters more when customers subscribe.
* You have presence. You can walk into a room with senior leaders, hold your view and argue it well.
* You lead with kindness. You’re strong, but you’re a mentor, not a dictator, and you collaborate well across teams.
* You’re resilient. It’s fast and high-pressure, and you’ll thrive on that rather than just survive it.

**Why it’s worth it**

You’ll have full ownership of a channel that drives most of the business’s revenue, and a direct line to the C-suite. The business is expanding internationally, and the leadership team expects its heads of to become directors. There’s budget behind it too.

**Good to know**

The office is in East Sussex and the role is 4 days a week on site. Please think honestly about the commute (in February, not September) before applying. If you’re in Brighton or Sussex, it’s an easy one.

# Senior Information Security Consultant (OT)

**Who you’ll be joining**

We’re problem solvers at heart. Sometimes the answer is technology, sometimes it is strategy, and sometimes it is a strong cup of tea and a bit of thoughtful conversation. Whatever it takes, we work it out with our clients.

We’re an IT consultancy that helps organisations get the best out of their technology. That means keeping them secure and keeping the bad guys out, making sure everything works and is easy to use, and doing smart things with data and software to give their business an edge. It is important work, and we care about doing it well and for the right reasons.

Life at Waterstons is friendly, flexible and built on trust. We hire people who are curious, thoughtful and good at getting to the heart of a problem. The unlimited holidays and private healthcare are a nice touch, although most people stay because it feels like the right place to do good work with good people.

As a Senior Information Security Consultant, you'll have an advanced understanding of, and over 5 years experience working with, organisations that have OT networks and standards used in the energy sector, such as the Cyber Assessment Framework and IEC ISA 99/62443.

You’ll be helping multiple clients with different aspects of their security. The role is interesting and varied and a great opportunity for those that prefer spontaneity over routine.

* Perform OT security assessments, gap analysis and risk assessments against recognised frameworks and standards.
* Develop pragmatic recommendations that improve cyber resilience while supporting operational requirements.
* Produce high-quality reports, presentations and client-facing deliverables.
* Build trusted relationships with client stakeholders across both operational and technology teams.
* Support proposal development, bids and client growth opportunities.
* Mentor junior consultants and contribute to knowledge sharing across the cyber team.
* Work closely with Principal Consultants and senior leadership to develop Waterstons' OT security capability.

* Someone who enjoys a varied environment, sharing their knowledge and experience to support colleagues.

* CISM or CISA

* Experience with the Cyber Assessment Framework, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-82, IEC ISA 99/62443 and CIS Controls.
* Strong understanding of IT and OT security risks.
* Knowledge of the threat landscape.
* Security Check (SC) clearance
* Someone who is comfortable engaging with operational teams, engineers, security teams and senior stakeholders to communicate cyber security risks and recommendations effectively.

* A healthy work life balance with flexible and agile working being the norm
* Flexible holiday allowance, with a minimum of 30 days a year
* EV car scheme (salary sacrifice)
* Room to grow with supported development opportunities and sponsored training
* Enhanced family policies
* If you ever need it, company sick pay and life assurance
* Supported wellbeing with regular initiatives, an employee assistance programme and private medical insurance
* Flexible benefits such as a dental scheme, eye care support, season ticket loan and cycle to work

Due to the nature of our work and the industries we support, all colleagues are required to successfully complete appropriate background security screening. Some client engagements may require Security Check (SC) clearance, and colleagues must therefore be willing and eligible to undergo SC clearance where required.

Waterstons is committed to creating and an inclusive, understanding, and flexible place to work. # Operations Rotation Scheme

## Join the Wild Side of Operations, rotating between Wild's Operations teams on an 18-month scheme. If you're ambitious, eager, and looking for an entry-level operations role, you should apply now!

#### **About us**

Hi there 👋 We're Wild. We set out to remove single-use plastic from the bathroom and ended up building one of the fastest-growing personal care brands in Europe. Our refillable, natural deodorant is now in millions of hands, our cases are collected like accessories, and our collaborations - from Disney to seasonal scent drops - keep the brand fresh, playful and impossible to ignore. Now part of the Unilever family, we have the backing to go global while keeping the pace, ambition and mischief of a start-up.

#### **🚀The Role**

***We’re looking for a curious, proactive and ambitious Operations Executive to join our rotational programme, designed to develop the next generation of operations talent and explore the*** ***Wild side of operations******.***

Rather than specialising in one function from day one, you’ll spend six months working within each of our three core Operations teams: Planning, Warehousing & Logistics, and Customer Experience. You’ll gain hands-on experience across the full operational lifecycle, learning how each function works individually and how they come together to deliver for our customers and the wider business.

You will take ownership of real projects and day-to-day responsibilities within each rotation, working alongside experienced team members to understand our processes, solve problems and identify opportunities to improve how we operate. You’ll also develop a strong understanding of the commercial and operational trade-offs involved in running a fast-growing consumer business.

By the end of the programme, you’ll have a holistic understanding of our Operations function, a broad network across the business and the skills to take on greater responsibility. The programme is intended to provide a strong foundation for a future career in Operations, with the opportunity to progress into a more specialised role based on your strengths, interests and business needs.

***Please note, this is an entry-level role.***

#### **⚡️What you'll do**

**Your responsibilities will evolve with each rotation, but will include:**

##### **1. Demand Planning**

Learn how we forecast customer demand and translate sales trends, commercial plans and market opportunities into an accurate view of future requirements.

* Support demand forecasting activities, analysing historical sales, trends, seasonality and promotional plans.
* Monitor forecast accuracy and bias, investigating variances between forecast and actual performance.
* Work with Commercial, Marketing and Retail teams to understand upcoming launches, promotions and channel growth.
* Help identify changes in demand and assess their potential impact on inventory availability.
* Build reports and dashboards to improve forecast visibility and support data-driven decision-making.
* Contribute to improvements in forecasting processes, reporting and planning tools.

##### **2. Supply Planning**

Learn how we translate demand forecasts into supply plans, ensuring the right products are available in the right quantities, at the right time, while balancing service levels, inventory investment and cost.

* Support supply planning and replenishment activities, helping translate demand forecasts into purchasing and production requirements.
* Monitor inventory levels, weeks of cover, safety stock and stock availability to identify risks and opportunities.
* Help manage purchase orders and track supplier delivery commitments against required dates.
* Identify potential stock-outs, excess inventory and supply constraints, working with relevant teams to develop mitigation plans.

# Chief Transformation Officer

## Job Introduction

We’ve made the investment. **Now it’s your opportunity to make the most of it.**

 

We’ve introduced new systems. Changed processes. Redesigned structures. Cleaned up our data. Started to change how we work. And made some significant investments along the way. So, as a truly Yorkshire based organisation naturally, we’d quite like to **squeeze every bit of value out of the investment we’re making****.**

Enter our new **Chief Transformation Officer**. 

At Yorkshire Housing, we’re on a mission to become the UK’s best housing provider. Yep. **Not exactly a small ambition.**

And the good news is, we’ve already made significant progress. We’ve invested in stronger data foundations, Azure, Salesforce, Workday and wider transformation activity, creating a much better platform for where we want to go next.

But the transformation is far from complete. Some of our most complex, business-critical work is still ahead of us.

So, here’s the important bit. **We’re not starting from scratch.**

**So where are we now?**

We’ve built strong foundations, but there’s still substantial technical, data and transformation work ahead. The next phase is about turning that investment into real results and supporting our move towards becoming a more pre-emptive organisation.

That means:

* developing Salesforce and strengthening our digital services
* making better use of data and AI to spot needs earlier and make better decisions
* building the integrated Data Lakehouse that will power our business intelligence
* moving safely away from legacy systems while improving the customer and colleague experience.

Salesforce will be a big part of that, but this is bigger than one platform. We need a joined-up architecture that connects our systems, data and services — and clear technical leadership to make it happen.

Technology. Culture. Data. Processes. People. **It all needs to work together.** And that’s where you come in.

**So, what’s the job?**

Our Chief Transformation Officer is a shiny new role we’ve added to our superstar Executive Team. You’ll bring the **technology, data and digital expertise** , alongside the strategic leadership, cultural change, challenge and assurance needed for the next phase of our transformation.

In Yorkshire terms?

**You’ll be the glue that turns transformation into results.**

So, here’s what you’ll be focussed on:

* join the dots between our strategy, technology, insight, people and processes, providing executive oversight, challenge and assurance across the transformation
* design and oversee the technology, data and integration architecture for the next phase, ensuring Salesforce and our wider platforms work together seamlessly for customers and colleagues
* lead the technical delivery of assets, rents, service charges and building safety compliance, including the safe migration away from legacy systems
* lead the creation of our integrated Data Lakehouse, turning the insight it enables into better decisions, earlier action and more pre-emptive services
* shape the capability and operating model needed to support our remaining on-premise infrastructure while building strong SaaS and cloud-platform management
* embed our Target Operating Model, Culture Programme and new ways of working, making a pre-emptive mindset part of everyday delivery rather than an ambition on a page
* realise the full value of the investments we’ve already made, working collaboratively with our Board, Executive Team and brilliant subject-matter experts across Yorkshire Housing.

Here’s the thing. This is a transformation role with technology, data and culture at its core. You’ll bring the technical credibility to lead complex architecture, migration and integration decisions, challenge specialists and partners, and ensure our platforms are resilient, connected and fit for the future.

As we rely more on cloud and SaaS platforms, you’ll build the capability, operating model and support needed to run them brilliantly.

**Spoiler alert — technology isn’t the answer to everything.** You’ll connect it with people, culture, insight and innovation, because brilliant systems alone don’t transform an organisation. **Transformation only counts if something actually transforms.**

**Who are we looking for?**

We’re looking for a proven technology leader who can operate at Executive and Board level and lead complex, organisation-wide transformation across technology, data, people, process and culture. You may have held a CTO, CIO or senior technology and transformation role. Whatever your title, you’ll bring substantial experience of architecture, enterprise platforms, data and digital delivery – and a track record of turning ambitious ideas into better, sustainable ways of working through changing the culture and mindset at a business wide level.

You might have worked in housing. **But you absolutely don’t need to have.**

And we’re far more interested in **what you’ve done,**than what your job title happened to be while you were doing it.

What we **do** need is someone who:

* has led complex transformation that brings together people, processes, insight and technology
* brings expertise in enterprise technology, data, digital and solution architecture
* has led complex migrations and integrations across business-critical platforms
* gets the people and culture side of transformation and can bring colleagues with them
* a proven track record of moving an organisation from reactive services towards anticipating needs and acting earlier
* understands modern data platforms and how to turn integrated data into actionable insight
* knows that supporting on-premise infrastructure and running cloud and SaaS platforms demand very different skills, and can build the capability and operating model needed for both through the transition
* can provide informed challenge and clear choices on technical risk, resilience, security, investment and delivery
* turns complexity into practical outcomes and communicates confidently with an Executive Team and Board
* understands benefits realisation and how to turn investment into genuine value

**And one more thing.**

**Leave the superhero cape at home.** We’ve already got brilliant people who know Yorkshire Housing, our customers and their specialist areas inside out. This isn’t about sweeping in with all the answers. It’s about bringing a fresh perspective and making the most of the expertise already here.

You’ll bring confidence without the ego, curiosity in bucketloads and a real knack for turning different perspectives into shared momentum. Because the real magic won’t come from one person having every answer. **It’ll come from getting the whole room moving in the same direction.**

If you know how to bring people together, unlock what’s already in the room and turn shared ambition into action, you’ll fit right in.

**Permanent? Fixed term? Fractional?**

**Potentially any of them.**

We’re deliberately keeping an open mind because we’d rather find the **right person** than rule them out because their preferred working arrangement doesn’t fit neatly into a box.

Maybe you’re looking for your next permanent executive role.

Maybe you want to come in, deliver something significant, make your mark and then pass the baton. **We’re happy to explore a range of options – the key is that we find the right person.**

 

**Why Yorkshire Housing?**

Because we’re ambitious, willing to think differently and honest enough to know we haven’t got everything figured out.

Behind the systems, data and transformation programmes is something much simpler: **making sure our customers have a safe place they’re proud to call home****.**

Our vision is to become the UK’s best housing provider — making better decisions, acting earlier and preventing avoidable problems. **Better outcomes for our customers.** That’s what all of this is ultimately about.

**How we’ll measure success**

Not by how many programmes you launch or how much new technology you buy, but by whether our investment is working together and customers can see the difference:

* our systems, data and services are connected and delivering what we need
* we use insight confidently to anticipate needs and act earlier
* our people work differently and the benefits are being realised
* Yorkshire Housing is **stronger, smarter and more capable because you were here.**

 

Sound like your kind of challenge?

**Watch our video from Chief Executive Nick Atkin to hear, in his own words, what we’re looking for and why this is such an important next step for Yorkshire Housing.**

Then, if you’re already mentally joining a few dots...

**We should probably talk.**

# Housing Officer
